rec.organizer: G. Franz, L. Hauswirth, P. Laurain, R. Petrides, R. Souam

rec.title: A mathematical perspective on Transformers
rec.speaker: Borjan GESHKOVSKI
rec.abstract: Physics has long supplied mathematics with some of its central equations. I will argue that Transformers, the engine of large language models, are becoming a source of the same kind. Starting from raw code, under various scaling assumptions, one can interpret Transformers as an interacting particle system in continuous time; tools from PDE and kinetic theory then explain empirically observed phenomena such as representation collapse and “lost in the middle”. Unlike in physics, however, the laws here are designed rather than given, so mathematical understanding can be written back into the architecture. I will close with some thoughts on what this two-way exchange means for applied mathematics.
rec.location_text: Sophie Germain, 1013
rec.organizer: G. Franz, L. Hauswirth, P. Laurain, R. Petrides, R. Souam

rec.title: The Spectral Gap for the Steklov Problem
rec.speaker: Asma HASSANNEZHAD
rec.abstract: We study the spectral gap for the Steklov problem on a Riemannian manifold. When a manifold has only one boundary component, it is known that the geometry of a boundary collar alone can provide a lower bound on the spectral gap. We therefore focus on manifolds with at least two boundary components. We show how the interior geometry can influence the spectral gap and establish a new connection between Steklov spectral gaps and the Neumann eigenvalues of interior subdomains. We then discuss applications of this connection to negatively curved manifolds. It is based on joint work with Tirumala Chakradhar and Bruno Colbois.
rec.location_text: Sophie Germain, 1013
rec.organizer: G. Franz, L. Hauswirth, P. Laurain, R. Petrides, R. Souam

rec.title: A Cartan Geometry from a Correspondence Space in Riemannian Geometry
rec.speaker: Rodrigo MORÓN SANZ
rec.abstract: Cartan geometries are curved analogues of homogeneous spaces, and the correspondence space construction produces, from a Cartan geometry of one type, another of a different type over a larger base manifold. The unit tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold is, in this language, a Cartan geometry of type (Euc(n), O(n-1)) obtained in this way; we study Cartan geometries of this type in general, whether or not they arise as correspondence spaces. We show that every such geometry induces on its base manifold an almost contact metric structure, together with an orthogonal splitting of the tangent bundle and a compatible linear connection; conversely, these data determine the geometry, so that the correspondence is a bijection. Moreover, we single out a distinguished Cartan connection, which we call normal, by a condition on its torsion formulated in terms of the Spencer differential. This normalization is dictated by the correspondence space construction: the Cartan connection induced on the unit tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold is normal.

rec.title: Model theory of limits
rec.speaker: Leo Gitin
rec.abstract:
We propose a model theory for directed limits and colimits of first-order structures, motivated by applications to commutative algebra and the model theory of valued fields. The treatment emphasises the natural assumption that transition maps are definable in a suitable sense.
Time permitting, I will explain connections to other approaches to this topic, including infinitary logic, Feferman’s local functors, ultraproducts, and pro- and ind-definable sets.

rec.title: Can you compute the operator norm in group C*-algebras?
rec.speaker: Isaac Goldbring
rec.abstract:
A paper by Fritz, Netzer, and Thom from 2012, titled "Can you compute the operator norm?", in essence initiated the computable structure theory for C*-algebras. The primary question involved is: given some "standard" presentation of a C*-algebra, is there an algorithm for computing the norm on the algebra? In this talk, I will focus on the case of C*-algebras arising from groups. In fact, most of the talk will focus on the case of the following four group C*-algebras: C^*(F_2), C^*(F_2\times F_2), C^*_r(F_2), C^*_r(F_2\times F_2). Here, for a group G, C^*(G) and C^*_r(G) denote the universal and reduced group C*-algebras associated to G, and F_2 denotes the free group on two generators. The answers to the question about computability of the norm for these four group C*-algebras turn out to be: yes, no, yes, and yes. The first is a result of FNT, the second a result due to myself and Thomas Sinclair from a year ago (answering a question of FN,T using recent results from quantum complexity theory), and the third and fourth recent results of mine (answering a question of Sinclair). Time permitting, I will discuss a potential generation of the latter results to wider classes of groups.
No prior knowledge of C*-algebra theory will be assumed.

rec.organizer: S. Anscombe, V. Bagayoko, H. Fournier

rec.title: A homotopy-theoretic approach to representation stability
rec.speaker: Nicolas Guès
rec.abstract:
In a series of papers from the 2010s, Church, Ellenberg and Farb developed the notion of representation stability, aimed at understanding the asymptotic behavior of natural sequences of representations of the symmetric groups S_n, particularly those arising from homological invariants. Such phenomena typically occur for FI-modules, i.e., functors from FI (the category of finite sets and injections) to abelian groups.
In this talk, I will propose a homotopical refinement of representation stability: a derived version adapted to (co)FI-spaces. This viewpoint sheds light on how the phenomenon of representation stability can arise from the high (co)cartesianity of certain cubical diagrams. With this point of view, I will show how one can deduce polynomial growth results for the homotopy groups of ordered configuration spaces on closed manifolds, recover the best known bounds on their cohomology, and generalize stability results of Palmer concerning moduli spaces of submanifolds.

rec.title: Braided module categories from small braidings
rec.speaker: Tyler Franke
rec.abstract: Braided module categories are module categories over braided monoidal categories equipped with extra structure providing an action of the braid group of the annulus on endomorphism spaces. In this talk, I will define a small braiding on an inclusion of monoidal categories, which provides a braiding between objects in these categories. Small braidings give certain tensor ideals the canonical structure of a braided module category. Quantum groups are a natural source of small braidings, and from this we construct concrete examples of braided module categories and quantum moment maps. I will outline how we plan to use these examples in skein-theoretic realisations of double affine Hecke algebras and certain modules thereof. Based on joint work-in-progress with Ingo Runkel and Volker Schomerus.

rec.speaker: Elden Elmanto
rec.abstract: The Milnor conjecture, a theorem of Kato and Voevodsky, asserts a close relation between bilinear forms, Milnor K-theory, Galois cohomology and differential forms defined over fields. I want to explain an extension of these results in mixed characteristics, building on work of Jacobson and obtained in joint work with Arnab Kundu which relies on recent development in syntomic and motivic cohomology.

rec.title: Condensed homotopy types in algebraic geometry, arithmetic geometry, and logic
rec.speaker: Peter Haine
rec.abstract:
Let X be a locally topologically noetherian scheme. In their paper on the proétale topology, Bhatt and Scholze defined the proétale fundamental group π1proét(X). The profinite completion of π1proét(X) recovers the usual étale fundamental group. Moreover, π1proét(X) agrees with π1ét(X) when X is normal, but π1proét(X) has the better property that it classifies Qp-local systems. In this talk, we’ll explain how to use condensed mathematics to define a “condensed homotopy type” whose fundamental group refines the proétale fundamental group. We’ll also talk about two related “condensed homotopy types”: one for adic spaces and one in the setting of logic. All three are special cases of a more general invariant of ∞-topoi. For adic spaces, the fundamental group refines the de Jong fundamental group, and in logic, the fundamental group recovers the Lascar group of a complete first-order theory.
These results come from several projects, carried out jointly with Holzschuh–Lara–Mair–Martini–Wolf, Achinger–Holzschuh–Lara–Mair–Wolf, and Damaj–Zhang.

rec.title: Topological freeness for minimal actions of groups with the rapid decay property
rec.speaker: Joseph Gondek
rec.abstract: We apply an operator-algebraic property of finitely generated groups, called rapid decay (RD), to topological dynamics. The class of groups with RD includes the hyperbolic groups and cocompact lattices in SL3(R), among many other examples. We show that the compact, minimal G-spaces of an RD group G with amenable neighbourhood stabilizers have some rigidity properties; under general conditions, all such actions are topologically free. This is joint work with Nazmul Alam, Mehrdad Kalantar, and Randy Pham.

rec.title: How to draw a module category: a glimpse into Auslander-Reiten theory
rec.speaker: Marius Goguet
rec.abstract:
Categories are often seen as very abstract mathematical objects that are hard to grasp. However, in the case of module categories of finite dimensional algebras, we can understand and represent them in a very concrete way by drawing their Auslander-Reiten quiver.
The general strategy is to break down the category into appropriate building blocks: indecomposable objects, irreducible morphisms and almost split sequences. We will define all these notions and illustrate them on examples of algebras given by quivers with relations.

rec.speaker: François Loeser
rec.abstract: In joint work with Antoine Ducros we provide a new proof, model-theoretic and geometric in nature, of the tame henselian rationality theorem of Kuhlmann. The proof takes place within the framework of stable completions of algebraic varieties over a valued field. It relies on two main results of independent interest: a Nash structure theorem for the stable completion of an algebraic curve and a tame descent theorem for abstract open polydiscs.

rec.title: Sard’s theorem in infinite dimension: from real algebraic geometry to sub-Riemannian geometry
rec.speaker: Antonio Lerario
rec.abstract:
Sard’s theorem can fail in infinite dimension, even for polynomial maps with finite-dimensional targets. I will explain how quantitative estimates in real algebraic geometry, combined with finite-dimensional approximation, yield Sard criteria in this setting. I will then show how Kupka’s classical counterexample can be realized inside a sub-Riemannian endpoint map. This produces a smooth bracket-generating distribution whose endpoint map has no regular values, disproving the sub-Riemannian Sard conjecture in the smooth category.
Based on joint works with Luca Rizzi and Daniele Tiberio.

rec.title: On the undecidability of the QWEP for C*-algebras
rec.speaker: Isaac Goldring
rec.abstract: In his landmark 1993 paper, Kirchberg introduced a property of C*-algebras called the QWEP, which stands for “quotient of the weak expectation property”. As the name suggests, the property is defined by the fact that the algebra is a quotient of a C*-algebra with the weak expectation property, which was a property introduced by Lance years earlier in connection with the theory of tensor products of C*-algebras. While at first glance this seems to be a strange property, Kirchberg showed that whether or not every C*-algebra has the QWEP is equivalent to the famous Connes Embedding Problem (CEP) from von Neumann algebra theory. The CEP remained open for nearly 50 years until its recent refutation in 2020 via a result in quantum complexity theory (as well as the equivalence with Kirchberg’s QWEP conjecture). Several years ago, I showed that the QWEP is an axiomatizable property of C*-algebras. In this talk, I will present joint work with Aruseelan and Hart where we show that the QWEP does not have an effective axiomatization and, in fact, there can be no effectively axiomatizable satisfiable theory of C*-algebras all of whose models have the QWEP (modulo some nontrivially conditions). The proofs uses the connection with the quantum complexity results mentioned above as well as other techniques from C*-algebra theory. No prior knowledge of continuous logic, operator algebras, or quantum complexity will be assumed.

rec.title: Algebraic Hodge-Generic Points and the Period Conjecture
rec.speaker: Gregorio Baldi
rec.abstract: Let f:X\to S be a quasi-projective family of varieties defined over Qbar. We prove that the points of S(Qbar) that are Hodge generic for the variation of Hodge structures associated to f are analytically dense in S. More generally, motivated by the Grothendieck period conjecture and under a large-monodromy assumption, we establish the density of algebraic points at which the periods of the fibre satisfy no unexpected relations of degree at most delta. The main technical input is a new result on relations among solutions of G-operators, based on height estimates of Bombieri and André. This is a joint work with Gal Binyamini and David Urbanik.

rec.title: Eliminating imaginaries in perfect, bounded, multi valued PAC fields
rec.speaker: Bryan Gonzalez Leandro
rec.abstract: Elimination of imaginaries is a fundamental structural property in model theory, which roughly means that definable equivalence classes can be coded by tuples of elements from the structure, allowing us to treat them as ordinary elements of the structure. In the context of valued fields, significant progress was initiated by Haskell, Hrushovski, and Macpherson, who described a language in which the theory ACVF eliminates imaginaries. Building on this foundation, Rideau-Kikuchi and Montenegro proved elimination of imaginaries for bounded pseudo p-adically closed fields equipped with finitely many independent valuations. In this talk, I will explain how their techniques can be adapted to prove weak elimination of imaginaries for perfect bounded PAC fields equipped with finitely many independent valuations. The strategy combines an extension theorem for types to invariant types with an amalgamation result.

rec.title: Constructing actions with Fraïssé limits
rec.speaker: Paolo Boldrini
rec.abstract: Given an action of a countable group on the Cantor space, clopen subsets can be compared by cutting and moving through the action or by evaluating them on invariant measures. Dynamical comparison asserts that the measure-theoretic notion controls the dynamical one. Since its first appearance, dynamical comparison has been verified for a wide variety of actions. In this talk, I will survey some recent positive results in this direction and present the construction of the first examples of topologically free minimal actions that fail dynamical comparison, obtained in a joint work with Akshara Prasad. The construction is based on an algebraic invariant known as the type semigroup and involves Fraïssé limits of Boolean algebras equipped with monoid-valued measures.

rec.title: F-CohFTs, their Givental group and tautological relations
rec.speaker: Paolo Rossi
rec.abstract: F-CohFTs are the natural generalization of cohomological field theories (CohFTs) when moving from the Deligne- Mumford compactification of the moduli space of stable curves given by nodal stable curves to the partial compactification given by curves with only separating nodes. They are natural under various viewpoints and were inspired by integrable systems considerations. As it happens for CohFTs, F-CohFTs can be used to probe the cohomology of this partial compactification, based on an analogue of the Givental-Teleman classification of semisimple CohFTs and similar nonsemisimple limiting techniques.

rec.title: Curve counting through intrinsic mirror symmetry
rec.speaker: Michel van Garrel
rec.abstract: According to Mirror Symmetry, the generating function of curve counting Gromov-Witten invariants of a Calabi-Yau threefold is conjectured to equal the integral over the positive real locus of a mirror-dual family of Calabi-Yau threefolds. In this joint work with Siebert, we prove that this conjecture holds as stated in the case of the canonical bundle of the projective plane with its mirror family constructed via the intrinsic mirror construction of Gross-Siebert. A key feature of the proof is that at no point do we calculate any invariants. Instead, we work with the punctured Gromov-Witten invariants that govern the intrinsic mirror construction.

rec.title: Torus actions on compactified braid varieties and polytopality of subword complexes
rec.speaker: Mikhail Gorsky
rec.abstract:
Every cluster variety admits a faithful regular group action scaling all cluster variables. Given a partial compactification of a cluster variety, a natural question is whether this action extends to a regular action on the compactification. I will explain that, in the case of braid varieties for simple Lie groups, the answer is affirmative for brick compactifications. If the braid variety is an open Richardson variety in the flag variety, the same result holds for the corresponding closed Richardson variety. In the latter case, the faithfully acting group is a torus of rank the Kazhdan-Lusztig d-invariant. The same result holds for projected Richardson varieties. I will also explain that, in general, a braid variety is a torus if and only if each of its brick compactifications is a toric variety with respect to this extended action, if and only if the polar dual of the moment polytope for this action realizes the corresponding subword complex. The braid words satisfying this property turn out to be precisely the double root free words of V. Pilaud and C. Stump. This provides a novel approach to the longstanding open question of the polytopality of spherical subword complexes asked by A. Knutson and E. Miller in 2004, and in particular gives infinite families of subword complexes admitting polytopal realizations in dimension higher than the rank of the corresponding Coxeter group. The talk is based on joint work with Lara Bossinger and José Simental, arXiv:2609.12414.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.

rec.title: "Quantum'' rational numbers, q-deformed Coxeter friezes, and the cross-ratio
rec.speaker: Valentin OVSIENKO
rec.abstract:
The classical cross-ratio ``crosses'' both classical and modern mathematics, linking geometry with combinatorics, dynamics, and mathematical physics. It provides natural coordinates on many moduli spaces. In this talk, I will introduce a new q-deformed, or ``quantum'' cross-ratio: a PSL(2,Z)-invariant of ordered quadruples of distinct points on the rational projective line. The construction is based on the theory of q-deformed rational numbers developed jointly with Sophie Morier-Genoud. I will discuss several properties of this new invariant, with its close connection to q-deformed Coxeter frieze patterns taking centre stage.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.

rec.title: Braid group invariance of quantum tori and applications
rec.speaker: Francesca Paganelli
rec.abstract:
A well-known fact in classical Lie theory is that the Weyl group W associated with a simple, complex, finite-dimensional Lie algebra g acts by isometries on the dual of the Cartan subalgebra. In particular, the symmetric bilinear form defined on the weight lattice is invariant under the W-action.
In this talk, I will present an analogue of this invariance phenomenon for skew-symmetric bicharacters in the context of quantum affine algebras. Specifically, we will consider the groups of fundamental and pre-fundamental l-weights (which can be viewed as affine analogues of the fundamental weights of g). By results of Chari and Frenkel–Hernandez, the braid group B associated with g acts on these groups of l-weights. We then introduce the skew-symmetric bicharacters on the groups of l-weights defined by Nakajima and Hernandez, and extended by Bittmann and myself. I will show that these bicharacters are invariant under the B-action on l-weight groups, and present an application concerning quantum QQ-systems in the theory of shifted quantum groups.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.

rec.title: Left Structures and Purity
rec.speaker: Kevin Schlegel
rec.abstract:

between its exact structures and certain closed subsets of the Ziegler spectrum of the ind-completion
of the category. This is based on a newly developed connection between exact structures and the theory
of purity. In fact, our results also apply to left structures, which vastly generalize exact structures.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.

rec.title: The Simplicial Cylinder DG Ring
rec.speaker: Amnon YEKUTIELI
rec.speaker_affiliation: Ben Gurion University, Israel et Université Paris 7
rec.abstract:
The Keller cylinder DG ring encodes homotopies between DG ring homomorphisms f_0, f_1 : A --> B.
Recently we discovered the higher cylinder DG rings Cyl_q(B), which assemble into the simplicial cylinder DG ring Cyl(B). For q=1 this recovers Keller's original construction.
The sets SHom_q(A,B) of DG ring homomorphisms A \to Cyl_q(B) form the simplicial Hom set SHom(A,B). Our main result is that when A is a semi-free DG ring, the simplicial set SHom(A,B) is a Kan complex.
We prove several results about the fundamental groupoid SHom_{\leq 1}(A,B), including invariance under quasi-isomorphism B' \to B, and that the automorphism groups are abelian. We also indicate some applications of this work, including to DG categories.
This talk will take place on Zoom only.

rec.title: Cohomologie étale des algèbres de Stein.
rec.speaker: Olivier Benoist
rec.abstract: Les variétés de Stein sont les analogues, en géométrie analytique complexe, des variétés algébriques affines. Je présenterai une version du théorème de comparaison d'Artin dans ce cadre : la cohomologie singulière à coefficients finis d'une variété de Stein est isomorphe à la cohomologie étale de son algèbre de fonctions holomorphes globales. Comme application, je montrerai que toute classe de cohomologie entière de degré au moins 2 sur une variété de Stein est supportée sur un sous-ensemble analytique strict. Les preuves combinent des outils de géométrie algébrique et de géométrie analytique.
rec.location_text: ENS, ENS salle W

rec.title: Weight functions on the Berkovich affine line over any non-Archimedean field
rec.speaker: Michael Maex
rec.abstract:
The theory of weight functions by Mustaţă-Nicaise on Berkovich spaces hints at an intrinsic approach to studying skeleta without the limitations of the usual tools from algebraic geometry, i.e., semistable reduction or resolution of singularities. In this talk we discuss how Mustaţă-Nicaise's construction can be generalised to define weight functions intrinsically on any quasi-smooth Berkovich space as a sort of normalised log-discrepancy of a canonical form.
Next, we turn our attention to computing weight functions on the Berkovich affine line over any non-Archimedean field K. This question reduces to the entirely value-theoretic problem of describing the integral log differentials $\Omega^{\log}_{L^\circ / K^\circ}$ for a simple extension of real valued fields $L / K$ , which we describe using the data in MacLane-Vaquié chains.
We find that on the affine line, weight functions are completely determined by the integral piecewise linear (Z-PL) structure the affine line and vice versa, yielding new insight into the Z-PL structure.
Finally, we discuss how this can be used to define and compute the essential skeleton of certain Berkovich spaces.

rec.title: Origami Tori
rec.speaker: Richard Schwartz
rec.abstract: An origami torus is a piecewise affine isometric embedding of a flat torus into R^3. It is surprising that these things exist, but they have been known to exist since 1960. How many vertices do you need to make an origami torus? In my talk, I will explain my proof that you can do it with 8 but not with 7. I will also explain why almost every flat torus is isometric to an origami torus -- this is joint work with Peter Doyle. If time permits I will also explain why, in fact, every flat torus is isometric to an 8-vertex origami torus. This is upcoming work with Doyle, Fabian Lander, and Steve Trettel.

rec.title: Séparer les composantes des variétés algébriques réelles par des invariants cohomologiques.
rec.speaker: Samuel Lerbet
rec.abstract: Si X est une variété algébrique complexe, il suit du théorème de comparaison de M. Artin que X et son lieu complexe X(C) ont le même nombre de composantes connexes, la première pour la topologie de Zariski, le second pour la topologie analytique ou forte. Au contraire, si X est une variété algébrique réelle connexe, son lieu réel X(R) est disconnexe pour la topologie forte en général. On peut néanmoins se demander si l'on peut séparer les composantes connexes de X(R) par des invariants algébriques de X. On peut pour cela utiliser des invariants de nature cohomologique : ainsi, E. Witt a montré que le signe des classes dans le groupe de Brauer d'une courbe algébrique réelle lisse séparent les composantes connexes de son lieu réel. La possibilité d'une telle séparation par un invariant cohomologique de degré donné dépend cependant de la relation entre ce dernier et la dimension : cela motive l'étude de l'optimalité de ce degré pour une dimension donnée. Le but de l'exposé est d'expliquer des résultats autour de cette question pour la séparation par la cohomologie et par son raffinement non ramifié et, si le temps le permet, des applications à la signature globale des formes quadratiques. Il s'agit d'un travail en commun avec Olivier Benoist.

rec.title: Positivité et sommes de carrés
rec.abstract: En 1927, Artin résout le 17ème problème de Hilbert en montrant que tout polynôme réel qui ne prend que des valeurs positives est une somme de carrés de fractions rationnelles. Mais combien de carrés sont nécessaires ? Cette question quantitative sera le fil conducteur de l’exposé. Je l’aborderai dans le cadre classique des polynômes réels, ainsi que dans des variantes arithmétiques et analytiques, en présentant quelques problèmes ouverts et des développements récents.

rec.title: Sur l´homologie asymptotique des graphes Lagrangians. (Avec Alfonso Sorrentino)
rec.speaker: Rafael Ruggiero
rec.abstract: Nous demontrons que les directions homologiques asymptotiques des orbites dans un graphe Lagrangien invariant par un flot Hamiltonien de Tonelli dans le tore au dessus du niveau critique de Mañé sont contenues dans un cône positif dans la norme stable autour d´un vecteur dans le premier group d'homologie à coefficients réels. En dimension 3, nous trouvons un rapport entre l´homologie asymptotique d´un graphe Lagrangien invariant et l´ensemble de rotation de Misiurewicz-Ziemann. Comme application, nous demontrons qu´il n'existent pas de graphes de Hedlund dans le 3-tore, ceux-ci sont des graphes avec exactement 3 orbites périodiques dont l´homologie engendre le premier group d´homologie.

rec.title: Centre des super-algèbres de Lie affines et des opérateurs pseudo-différentiels
rec.speaker: Shigenori Nakatsuka
rec.abstract:
Dans la théorie des représentations, le centre des algèbres
elles-mêmes joue un rôle fondamental. Par exemple, le centre des
algèbres enveloppantes des algèbres de Lie réductives a été décrit par
Harish-Chandra, permettant la décomposition en blocs de la catégorie O.
Dans le cas affine, Feigin et Frenkel ont identifié le centre à
l’algèbre des fonctions sur l’espace des opérateurs différentiels.
Frenkel et Gaitsgory l’ont ensuite utilisé pour décrire la catégorie O
sphérique, l’un des premiers résultats de la correspondance de
Langlands géométrique locale.
Dans mon exposé, je présenterai des résultats sur les super-algèbres
de Lie affines, en particulier pour le cas gl(n|m). Dans ce contexte,
les opérateurs pseudo-différentiels apparaissent naturellement. Si le
temps le permet, j’expliquerai également l’intérêt de considérer le
cadre super et le cas en général.
Ce travail est basé sur des collaborations avec D. Adamović et B. Feigin.

rec.title: Projective curves and Peano Arithmetic
rec.speaker: Alessandro Berarducci
rec.abstract: Joint work with Francesco Gallinaro. Addressing a question of Marcus Tressl, we study the structure Var(C) given by the incidence relation between points and irreducible complex projective curves. We show that Var(C) is bi-interpretable with the polynomial ring C[x] and therefore it has an undecidable theory, as it interprets both C and the subring Z of integers. Nevertheless Var(C) is tame modulo the integers, in the sense that a copy Z of the ring of integers is stably and conservatively embedded in Var(C), all types are controlled by the integers, and the theory of Var(C) is recursively axiomatizable over the complete theory of Z. By contrast, we do not know whether Var(R) is undecidable, or whether it interprets R, where R is the real field and Var(R) is defined like Var(C) but considering only the real points. Replacing C with the field K of complex algebraic numbers yields a structure Var(K) that is not elementary equivalent to Var(C) but it is again recursively axiomatizable over Z. Our results depend on a bi-interpretation of Var(C) with the two-sorted structure (C,Fin(C)) consisting of the field C and a sort for its finite subsets, with the membership relation between the two sorts.

rec.title: Nonexistence of homomorphisms between matrix algebras over spheres which are injective on K-theory
rec.speaker: Chris Phillips
rec.abstract:
Résumé : This is joint work with Ilan Hirshberg.
In 1993, Blackadar asked for which $n$, $k$, $d$, and $r$ there is a unital homomorphism $C (S^{2 n}, M_r) \to C (S^{2 k}, M_{d r})$ which is injective on $K_0$. There are "obvious" examples constructed as follows. For $m \in {\mathbb{N}}$, $K^1 (S^{2 m - 1})$ is generated by the class of a unitary in $C (S^{2 m - 1}, M_m)$, and from this one gets homomorphisms $C (S^{1}) \to C (S^{2 m - 1}, M_m)$ which are injective on $K_1$. One can then take (odd) suspensions, increase the matrix size in the codomain, and tensor everything with $M_r$. Ordered $K_0$ suggests that many more might exist. In particular, Blackadar asked whether there is a unital homomorphism $C (S^{2 n}, M_{2 n}) \to C (S^{4 n}, M_{4 n})$ which is injective on $K_0$.
The answer is no. We prove that the only choices of $n$, $k$, $d$, and $r$ for which such a homomorphism exists are those which occur in the examples above. The proof uses indecomposability in the rational cohomology ring of the space of homomorphisms from $C (S^{2 n})$ to $M_d$.
This material is based upon work partially supported by the US National Science Foundation under Grant DMS-2400332.

rec.title: Fomin-Kirillov algebras
rec.speaker: Leandro Vendramin
rec.abstract:
Fomin-Kirillov algebras EnE_nEn​ are quadratic algebras introduced by Fomin and Kirillov in the late 1990s to study the combinatorics of Schubert polynomials. They contain a commutative subalgebra isomorphic to the cohomology ring of the flag manifold, and they are related to Nichols algebras over the symmetric group. It has been known for some time that Fomin-Kirillov algebras EnE_nEn​ are finite-dimensional for n≤5n\leq 5n≤5, but whether this holds for n>5n>5n>5 has remained open since the algebras were introduced. In this talk, I will review basic properties of Fomin-Kirillov algebras and present joint work with Andruskiewitsch, Angiono, Heckenberger, Lentner, and Reiher, in which we prove that Fomin-Kirillov algebras EnE_nEn​ are infinite-dimensional for all n>5n>5n>5.
This talk will take place on Zoom only.

rec.title: Markov triples and tropical geometry
rec.speaker: Mikhail Shkolnikov
rec.abstract: Markov triples forming an infinite set of triples of natural numbers were introduced by Markov as a part of his study of relation between real binary quadratic forms and the square lattice. Frobenius conjecture, remaining open for more than one hundred years, has acquired numerous reformulations in various contexts; in its original formulation, it states that the maximal element of a Markov triple determines the remaining two numbers in this triple. In my talk, i will tell about two other equivalent statements in the tropical context recently obtained by Kevin Calderon: the first one is given via tropical cotangents of angles formed by two tangents to Markov hyperbolas, and the other one is a conjectural statement about tropical wave fronts of Markov triangles.

rec.title: Combinatorics, Arithmetic and Geometry working group: Shkolnikov, Kartas, Wang
rec.abstract:
11:30-12:20: Mikhail Shkolnikov (ICMS Sofia)
Title: Combinatorial and Geometric aspects of Tropical Optics
Abstract: This talk is dedicated to an introduction and an overview of the current status of the theory of tropical wave fronts and their caustics seen from toric perspective. Particular emphasize will be made on the ongoing finite-time analysis of the structure of critical events in the tropical wave front propagation operating on convex polyhedra and the role of corresponding algebro-geometric singularities in the character of this canonical evolution as being developed in joint project with Grigory Mikhalkin. We will finish with discussing the fundamental open problem of understanding possible pre-final moments of such an evolution, which is fully resolved only in dimension 2, with final moments now being classified in all dimensions.
15:00-15:50: Konstantinos Kartas (Université de Paris-Saclay)
Title: Taming perfectoid algebras
Abstract: The almost purity theorem is a foundational result about perfectoid algebras which, as the name suggests, holds only in an "almost" sense. We show that suitable completeness hypotheses on the algebras allow us to remove the "almost". More precisely, spherically complete perfectoid algebras satisfy non-almost purity for Galois p-extensions and countably saturated perfectoid algebras satisfy non-almost purity for all finite étale extensions. Joint work with Franziska Jahnke.
16:00-16:50: Yiyu Wang (Ohio State University)
Title: Grothendieck weight on permutohedral varieties and matroids
Abstract: Minkowski weights provide a combinatorial model for the Chow ring of smooth toric varieties. In this talk, I will introduce their K-theoretic analogue, the Grothendieck weights, and describe them explicitly for permutohedral varieties. Our results include a balancing condition and a product rule for Grothendieck weights. These results give a concrete way to work in the K-ring of the permutohedral variety.
I will then discuss applications to matroids, where many naturally occurring K-classes admit simple descriptions in terms of Grothendieck weights. In particular, I will explain how the motivic Chern class of a hyperplane arrangement complement in its wonderful model only depends on its underlying matroid.
If time permits, I will briefly mention some further applications of Grothendieck weights to positivity questions in matroid K-theory.

rec.title: Singularities of the critical wave equation and the Keller-Segel system formed by the collision of collapsing solitons at a point
rec.speaker: Charles Collot
rec.abstract: Critical evolution PDEs may have solutions forming a singularity in finite time with anomalous self-similarity. There are now numerous examples where a soliton (here a stationary state or a traveling wave) collapses at a point due to its interactions with the remainder of the solution. Much less is known about singularities formed by several solitons collapsing simultaneously at a single point, especially in the non-radial case. The first example was constructed for the nonlinear Schrodinger equation by Martel-Raphael [Ann. Sci. ENS 2018]. I will present examples of such solutions for the parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system in two dimensions [joint work with Ghoul-Masmoudi-Nguyen 2024] and for the cubic wave equation in four dimensions [ongoing joint work with Li to appear]. The associated patterns are caused by different effects for each equation: the solitons' own dynamics, their interactions, and their interactions with the remainder of the solution which is affected by the presence of the multiple nearby potentials from the solitons. I will present ideas for the construction of an approximate solution, and its stability analysis based on the control of its modulating parameters and of suitable norms for the remainder, adapted to the multiscale feature of the problem.

rec.title: Scary Wheels (and Super Shrubs)
rec.speaker: Andrei Negut
rec.abstract: Together with Alexander Tsymbaliuk, we propose a blueprint for constructing shuffle realizations of various quantum loop (super)algebras; this is a valuable tool for the study of these important algebraic structures and their representation theory. We apply this framework to the case of classical super-types A,B,C,D, which leads us into new combinatorics: higher order wheel conditions on one hand, and on the other hand certain generalizations of Young diagrams that we call shrubs (in types A) and asps (in types B,C,D).

rec.title: Séminaires de doctorants
rec.speaker: Marius Kjaersgaard, Changjiang Du, Lucrezia Bertoletti, Marc Coulomb
rec.abstract:
14h - 14h25: Marius Kjaersgaard
Title: Local constancy of the Betti automorphic category over the moduli of curves
Abstract: Nadler and Yun have defined a relative notion of Betti automorphic sheaves and conjectured that they form a locally constant sheaf of categories over the moduli space of curves. We give a brief overview of the conjecture and work in progress, joint with Joakim Færgeman, towards proving the conjecture.
14h30 - 14h55: Changjiang Du
Title: Multivariable (phi,Gamma)-modules associated to p-adic Galois representations
Abstract: Let K be a finite unramified extension of Q_p. In a series of works by Breuil, Herzig, Hu, Morra, and Schraen, a multivariable coefficient ring A was constructed, together with two functors: D_A^{\otimes}, which sends mod p Galois representations to étale (phi,Gamma)-modules over A, and D_A, which sends admissible smooth mod p representations of GL_2(K) to étale (phi,O_K*)-modules over A. In this talk, we will explain how to construct the p-adic analogue of D_A^{\otimes}. This construction relies on two descent arguments: the pro-étale descent for perfectoid spaces and the Frobenius descent for phi-modules.
15h - 15h25: Lucrezia Bertoletti
Title: Finite length for unramified GL2: beyond multiplicity one.
Abstract: For K a finite unramified extension of Qp, a natural place to look for a conjectural mod p Langlands correspondence for GL2(K) are Hecke eigenspaces in the mod p cohomology of a tower of Shimura curves, which are expected to be a direct sum of copies of a representation (i.e. depending only on the input at p of the global setting) of GL2(K). The expected number of copies, called the multiplicity, should then be computed by counting Serre weights in the socle.
In the multiplicity one case, a recent work of Breuil, Herzig, Hu, Morra and Schraen establishes the finite length of the above Hecke eigenspaces, under mild genericity assumptions.
In this talk we will discuss how to extend this finite length result when the multiplicity one assumption is removed.
15h30 - 15h55: Marc Coulomb
Titre : Développement asymptotique explicite et matrices de Stokes des E-fonctions hypergéométriques.
Résumé : La famille des E-fonctions hypergéométriques généralise les fonctions de Bessel, de Kummer, et est liée à de nombreuses fonctions spéciales. Le résultat principal est une formule close, explicite, donnant le développement asymptotique de ces fonctions dans tout grand secteur angulaire autorisé. De cette formule découlent la sommation explicite de Borel-Laplace des fonctions hypergéométriques divergentes, ainsi que les matrices de Stokes associées.

rec.title: Gelfand-Kirillov dimensions and the p-adic Langlands program
rec.speaker: Reinier SORGDRAGER
rec.abstract:
This thesis' main results are upper bounds to the Gelfand-Kirillov dimension of certain p-adic representations and some applications of such bounds.
The Gelfand-Kirillov dimension is a generalization of the Krull dimension of modules ovef commutative rings to modules over completed group rings of p-adic Lie groups -- also known as Iwasawa algebras. These Iwasawa algebras act on the duals of p-adic Banach representations or smooth mod p representations of such groups.
The main result is, for p>2 a prime number, that an admissible p-adic Banach representation of GL_2 of a p-adic field K has Gelfand-Kirillov dimension at most the degree [K:Q_p] as soon as its locally analytic vectors admit an infinitesimal character.
The second main result is a generalization of this statement to families of Banach representations with infinitesimal characters in families in the sense of Dospinescu-Paškūnas-Schraen. This result yields a generalization of the GK-bound of Breuil-Herzig-Hu-Morra-Schraen beyond K unramified for the smooth mod p representation given by a Galois isotypic component in the mod p cohomology of Shimura varieties.
The method of proof for both results is much in the spirit of the filtrations of fixed ``radius of analyticity'' of Schneider-Teitelbaum on the duals of the representations and the study of their associated gradeds. The second main result required a generalization of these filtrations to double radii.
Finally, this thesis has two more results. The most important one being that (in the setting of K unramified, only needing the results of Breuil-Herzig-Hu-Morra-Schraen) the GK-bound for mod p cohomology of Shimura varieties allows one, via miracle flatness of the patched module over R_\infty, to compute the derived pro-p Iwahori invariants of the mod p representation as complex over the non-derived pro-p Iwahori Hecke algebra, up to quasi-isomorphism. This derived module turns out to depend only on the mod p Galois representation (and a multiplicity) and not on the global choices that go into the construction of the smooth mod p representation of GL_2.

rec.title: Reprojections des pavages par le Spectre et motifs hexagonaux
rec.speaker: Arnaud Chéritat
rec.abstract: L'une des monotuiles apériodiques découvertes en 2023 par Smith et al. est appelée spectre. On peut associer naturellement aux pavages par le spectre un relevé à $\mathbb{R}^4$ du graphe des arêtes du pavage. On peut faire de même avec un autre graphe, issu d'une décoration particulière de la tuile. En reprojetant ces graphes vers le plan selon différentes directions, on observe des motifs intéressants. rec.title: Monodromy in Radial Persistence Vineyards and visualizing with Bouquet2D
rec.speaker: Rohit Roy
rec.abstract:
Given a manifold M without boundary, the Radial Persistence Transform (RPT) assigns to each point x in R^2 the persistence diagram of the squared Euclidean distance function d_E^2(., x) restricted to M. As x moves along a closed loop gamma, these diagrams form a periodic vineyard. The RPT is a variant of the persistent homology transform (PHT) introduced by Turner and collaborators, and is more sensitive, see Onus et al. Both the RPT and PHT can exhibit monodromy; after a full traversal of gamma, points of the persistence diagram return permuted. Monodromy obstructs feature tracking and complicates downstream analysis in TDA pipelines, and understanding when and why it occurs is an open problem. Arya et al. gave an example with monodromy for the PHT and the geometric conditions that exclude monodromy, both in 2 dimensions.
Chambers et al. showed that monodromy and knotting of arbitrary complexity can occur for the RPT. We are exploring the relation between the monodromy in a vineyard and the topology of the vineyard for the RPT on one hand and the symmetry and focal set (the bifurcation set for distances) on the other. Classical results of Bruce, Giblin and Gibson, and of Porteous, show that the Morse decomposition of the distance function changes only when x crosses the symmetry set or the focal set of M. We prove that for curves in R^2, the vineyard of a sufficiently small loop gamma cannot exhibit monodromy unless gamma encloses a specific singularity of the symmetry set. This yields a local classification of the causes of monodromy in 2 dimensions, which we are currently expanding to a global classification. This opens the door to algorithmic criteria for detecting and then exploiting or avoiding it.
Our investigation has been informed and corroborated by experimentation with Bouquet2D, an interactive web-based tool for exploring this phenomenon. The tool allows the user to define M as a spline curve and draw a loop gamma, and the tool displays the symmetry and focal sets of M together with the vineyard as x moves along gamma. Deforming M updates all of these in real time, so one can directly observe how bifurcations of the symmetry and focal sets appear as events in the vineyard, and where monodromy arises. Bouquet2D is available for everyone to experiment with vineyard topology at: https://bouquet2d.rohitroy.me/.

rec.title: Colloquium : "Nielsen meets Weil"
rec.speaker: Maxim Kontsevich
rec.abstract: A hundred years ago Jacob Nielsen proposed a lower bound on the number of fixed points of a self-map, utilizing the action on the fundamental group. The natural bookkeeping device is the Reidemeister trace, a linear combination of twisted conjugacy classes. I will review the classical theory and propose an analogue for varieties over finite fields, in the spirit of the rationality part of the Weil conjectures, where the self-map is replaced by the Frobenius automorphism. The resulting conjecture can be checked in non-trivial examples.

rec.title: Conditions de stabilité à la Bridgeland et applications
rec.speaker: Vanja ZULIANI
rec.abstract:
Les conditions de stabilité à la Bridgeland nous permettent d’étudier les espaces de modules d’objets dans une catégorie dérivée et de décomposer chaque objet en facteurs plus “simples". Cette thèse examine deux applications de la théorie des conditions de stabilité à la Bridgeland. Dans la première partie, on étudie la géométrie d’une variété de Fano de dimension 8 et d’indice 3, définie comme une sousvariété lagrangienne d’une variété hyperkählérienne ; on étudie une dégénérescence semistable et on en déduit ses nombres de Hodge. En particulier, on observe que la structure de Hodge est de type K3 et que le rang de Picard est égal à un.
La deuxième application de la théorie des conditions de stabilité concerne l’étude du programme des modèles minimaux non commutatifs. On montre que les décompositions semiorthogonales standard sur les grassmanniennes, les quadriques et les hypersurfaces cubiques de dimension 3 et 4 sont induites par des chemins quasi-convergents dans la variété de stabilité, dont la charge centrale est donnée par la cohomologie quantique. Une partie du dernier chapitre est basée sur un travail en collaboration avec Tomohiro Karube et Antonios-Alexandros Robotis.
rec.location_text: IMO Orsay, 3L15

rec.title: Une inégalité isopérimétrique quantitative dans l'espace
rec.speaker: Gisella Croce
rec.abstract:
Dans ce séminaire nous allons étudier un problème de stabilité pour l'inégalité isopérimétrique dans $\mathbb{R}^3$, faisant intervenir une asymétrie de type Hausdorff. Pour un corps convexe $F \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ de volume $4\pi/3$ (c'est-à-dire le volume de la boule unité dans l'espace), nous considérons la fonctionnelle \[ Q^*(F) := \frac{\delta(F)\log\bigl(\delta(F)+\delta(F)^{-1}\bigr)P(F)^3} {\lambda^*(F)^2}, \] o\`u $\delta(F)$ d\'esigne le déficit isop\'erim\'etrique, c'est-à-dire la différence entre le périmétre $P(F)$ et le périmètre de la boule unité, et $\displaystyle \lambda^*(F):=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^3} d_H(F,B+x)$
la distance de Hausdorff à la famille des boules unit\'es. Le facteur logarithmique reflète l'échelle capacitaire optimale au voisinage de la boule en dimension trois, tandis que le facteur $P(F)^3$ assure la coercivité. Notre résultat principal est l'existence du minimum de $Q^*$ dans la classe des corps convexes de volume $4\pi/3$.
Ce travail est en collaboration avec S. Bove et G. Pisante.

rec.title: A Reider Theorem for Hilbert Schemes of Points on a Surface
rec.speaker: Aaron Bertram
rec.abstract: Reider's Theorem on very ampleness of divisors of the form \(K_S + D\) on a non-singular surface has a natural generalization to ampleness of divisors of the form \((K_S + D)_d - \Delta\) on the Hilbert schemes of d points on \(S\). The boundary case, where we can prove the divisor is nef but not ample, is a very natural generalization of the pull-back of \(2\Theta\) under the Abel-Jacobi map for curves. In light of Mumford's theorem for surfaces with \(p_g\) different from zero, these nef divisors surprised us. In this talk I will explain some interesting geometry for particular surfaces and also sketch the proof, which relies on results of Bayer-Macrì and Toda on Bridgeland stability conditions on surfaces.

rec.title: On the Wasserstein Geodesic Principal Component Analysis of probability measures
rec.speaker: Alice Le Brigant
rec.abstract:
The GdT OT-PDE-ML is a research seminar organized by the ParMA team. It brings together researchers to discuss recent theoretical and numerical developments at the crossroads of Optimal Transport theory, Partial Differential Equations and Machine Learning.
Abstract: In this talk we discuss how to perform Principal Component Analysis (PCA) of a dataset whose elements are probability distributions, compared using the Wasserstein distance. The goal is to identify geodesic curves in the space of probability measures that best capture the modes of variation of the underlying dataset. To achieve this, we leverage the Riemannian interpretation of the Wasserstein metric. We first address the case of a collection of centered Gaussian distributions, and show how to lift the computations in the space of invertible linear maps using Bures-Wasserstein geometry. For the more general setting of absolutely continuous probability measures, we use Otto-Wasserstein geometry and neural networks to parameterize geodesics in Wasserstein space. Finally, we compare to classical tangent PCA through various examples and provide illustrations on real-world datasets.

rec.title: Algèbres de von Neumann de réseaux arithmétiques et ensembles de Kakeya
rec.speaker: Mikael de la Salle
rec.abstract:
Une forme de la conjecture de rigidité de Connes prédit que les algèbres de von Neumann de $\mathrm{PSL_n}(Z)$ sont toutes distinctes. Au moment où j'écris ces lignes, cette conjecture est toujours ouverte. Des anciens travaux avec Vincent Lafforgue et Tim de Laat (ainsi que d'autres travaux de Uffe Haagerup et Tim de Laat) suggèrent une approche possible à cette conjecture, en terme de propriétés d'approximation.
J'expliquerai pourquoi cette approche est difficile: elle implique aussi une forme de la conjecture de Kakeya en toute dimension.
La conjecture de Kakeya en dimension d affirme que toute partie de l'espace euclidien de dimension d, qui contient un segment dans toute direction, est de dimension de Hausdorff égale à d. Au moment où j'écris ces lignes, cette conjecture est prouvée uniquement en dimension 2 (Davies, Cordoba) et 3 (Wang et Zahl).

rec.title: Hidden symmetries of modular geodesics
rec.speaker: Alain Valette
rec.abstract:
The dihedral group of order 4 acts on the conjugation classes of hyperbolic elements of $PSL_2(\mathbf{Z})$: by passage to the inverse, by conjugation by an element of $GL_2(\mathbf{Z})$ of determinant -1, and by the product of the 2. Via the dictionary (which will be recalled) between closed hyperbolic and geodesic conjugation classes of the modular surface, the same group acts on modular geodesics, which can therefore acquire non-trivial symmetries by being fixed under one of the 3 involutions above. We will characterize these invariant geodesics and we will see that there is a strong link with Gauss' reciprocal, ambiguous and inert quadratic forms. It is a joint work with C.-L. Simon (Rennes)

rec.title: Homogenized Transformers
rec.speaker: Hugo Koubbi
rec.abstract:
The GdT OT-PDE-ML is a research seminar organized by the ParMA team. It brings together researchers to discuss recent theoretical and numerical developments at the crossroads of Optimal Transport theory, Partial Differential Equations and Machine Learning.
Abstract: We study a random model of deep multi-head self-attention in which the weights are resampled independently across layers and heads, as at initialization of training. Viewing depth as a time variable, the residual stream defines a discrete-time interacting particle system on the unit sphere. We prove that, under suitable joint scalings of the depth, the residual step size, and the number of heads, this dynamics admits a nontrivial homogenized limit.Depending on the scaling, the limit is either deterministic or stochastic with common noise; in the mean-field regime, the latter leads to a stochastic nonlinear Fokker–Planck equation for the conditional law of a representative token. In the Gaussian setting, the limiting drift vanishes, making the homogenized dynamics explicit enough to study representation collapse. This yields quantitative trade-offs between dimension, context length, and temperature, and identifies regimes in which clustering can be mitigated.

rec.title: Régulateur cyclosyntomique des corps de nombres ~~ Transfer principles and the Kato–Kuzumaki conjecture
rec.speaker: Quentin Gazda, Felipe Gambardella
rec.abstract:
Felipe Gambardella (Orsay), 2-3pm
Transfer principles and the Kato–Kuzumaki conjecture.
Seeking a Diophantine characterisation of cohomological dimension of fields, Kato and Kuzumaki introduced the C_i^q property for every pair of non-negative integers i and q. These properties are inspired by Lang’s notion of a C_i field and Bloch-Kato’s conjecture relating Milnor K-theory with Galois cohomology. An interesting property of C_i fields is that they satisfy a transfer principle with respect to equicharacteristic complete discrete valuations – i.e. if a field k is C_i, then the field of Laurent series k((t)) is C_{i+1}. However, for the C_i^q property, no such transfer result is known to hold and the situation is more subtle than the one of C_i fields. For instance, the optimistic statement “k((t)) satisfies C_{i+1}^q whenever k satisfies C_i^q ” is false. This talk reports on joint work with Konstantinos Kartas. I will present a transfer principle for C_i fields with respect to non-discrete valuations. This principle has as a corollary a transfer principle for a variant of the Kato-Kuzumaki properties. Moreover, this is enough to establish the Kato-Kuzumaki conjecture for several fields of arithmetic interest such as the perfection of Fp((t_1)) . . . ((t_n)) or C(x_1, . . . , x_n)((t_1)) . . . ((t_m)) and to establish a strengthening of the C_1^1 property for Q_p introduced by Wittenberg.
Quentin Gazda (IMJ-PRG), 3.30-4.30pm
Régulateur cyclosyntomique des corps de nombres
Dans cet exposé, nous présenterons un travail en commun avec Tess Bouis où nous construisons une version q-déformée du régulateur de Dirichlet p-adique des corps de nombres. De manière surprenante, notre construction ne nécessite ni la complétion en p, ni que p soit premier. Nous interpréterons ce régulateur à travers la notion de q-Gauges, objets globaux ayant vocation à interpoler les structures de Hodge p-adiques en chaque p.

rec.title: Introduction to circle-packings
rec.speaker: Jules Duhamel
rec.abstract:
Le séminaire des doctorants se propose de fournir aux doctorants une occasion de s'ouvrir aux autres domaines des mathématiques que le leur. A chaque séance, un intervenant réalise un exposé sur un fait standard de leur domaine d'étude, de niveau adapté à l'ensemble des doctorants.
Introduction aux empilements de cercles
Le théorème des empilements de cercles (circle-packings) est un théorème très amusant et dont la preuve est élémentaire. Il permet d'associer un empilement de cercles à toute triangulation simple et planaire. Ce théorème a été découvert indépendamment à trois reprises, à chaque fois pour des motifs différents. Ce n'est qu'après une conférence donnée par Thurston en 1985 que la communauté mathématique se saisit des empilements de cercles. L'objectif de l'exposé est de présenter une preuve du théorème et quelques-unes de ses multiples applications.
----
The PhD students seminar aims to provide PhD students with an opportunity to explore other areas of mathematics beyond their own. At each session, a speaker gives a presentation on a standard topic in their field of study, at a level suitable for all phd students.
The circle-packing theorem is a very fun theorem whose proof is elementary. It associates a circle-packing to any simple planar triangulation. This theorem was independently discovered three times, each time with different motives. In 1985, Thurston gave a talk on the subject which is responsible for the growth of interest for circle-packings in the mathematical community. The goal of the talk is to give a proof of the theorem together with a few of its numerous applications.

rec.title: Plongements conformes de surfaces de Riemann
rec.speaker: Alaa Mohamed BOUKHOLKHAL
rec.abstract: Étant donnée une surface riemannienne, il n’est pas toujours possible de la plonger isométriquement dans une variété riemannienne donnée M, notamment en raison de contraintes telles que la courbure. Cependant, la situation devient beaucoup plus flexible si l’on cherche un plongement conforme. Dans cet exposé, on montre l’existence de plongements conformes dans le cas où M est une variété pseudo-riemannienne. De plus, on montre que l’inclusion de l’espace des immersions lisses et conformes dans l’espace des immersions induit une bijection entre les composantes connexes par arcs de ces deux espaces.

rec.title: Géométries de Wasserstein slicées et hiérarchiques : flots de gradient et analyse variationnelle
rec.speaker: Christophe Vauthier
rec.abstract: Dans cette thèse, nous analysons la géométrie induite par deux variantes de la distance de Wasserstein en transport optimal: la distance de Sliced-Wasserstein, et la distance Wasserstein sur Wasserstein. Dans la première partie de cette thèse, nous nous focalisons sur la distance de Sliced-Wasserstein, et nous examinons les propriétés de convergence et les points critiques de sa forme semi-discrète. Puis, nous définissons un cadre général pour l'étude de points critiques de fonctionnelles définies sur des espaces de mesures de probabilités, que nous utilisons pour démontrer que les points critiques en contexte semi-discret sont un cas particulier d'un type spécifique de mesures critiques que nous appelons points critiques lagrangiens. Nous étudions ensuite les propriétes des points critiques lagrangiens de la distance de Sliced-Wasserstein, notamment leur existence et leur stabilité. Enfin, nous étudions la quantification de la distance de Sliced-Wasserstein, et nous dérivons de nouvelles bornes sur son erreur de quantification uniforme. Dans la deuxième partie de cette thèse, nous nous concentrons sur le cas particulier du transport optimal où l'espace sous-jacent est lui-même un espace de probabilités. Nous construisons en particulier une structure de type riemannien sur l'espace de mesures de probabilités sur des mesures de probabilités $\cPP{\R^d}$, muni de la distance Wasserstein sur Wasserstein, nous permettant de considérer des flots de gradient Wasserstein sur cet espace. Nous montrons ensuite comment ce cadre théorique peut être appliqué à divers problèmes de machine learning, par le biais de flots de jeux de données représentés par des éléments de $\cPP{\R^d}$. Enfin, dans la troisième et dernière partie, nous étendons cette théorie à toute la suite d'espaces $\cPn{n}{\cM} = \cP_2(\ldots\cP_2(\cM)\ldots)$ obtenue en itérant l'opération $\cP_2$ sur une variété riemannienne $\cM$. Nous montrons que ces espaces peuvent à nouveau être munis d'une structure de type riemannien d'une façon systématique, nous permettant d'analyser leur géométrie, de caractériser leurs géodésiques et de définir le gradient de fonctionnelles.

rec.title: Points critiques stationnaires pour un modèle champ de phase en mécanique de la rupture
rec.speaker: Martin Rakovsky
rec.abstract: Cette thèse est consacrée à la fonctionnelle de Mumford-Shah, utilisée pour modéliser les fissures fragiles dans un matériau élastique, et plus particulièrement à son approximation par la fonctionnelle d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli. Nous nous intéressons notamment à l'analyse asymptotique des points critiques de la fonctionnelle d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli, afin d'étendre aux points critiques la convergence des minimiseurs globaux obtenue par $Gamma$-convergence. Nous commençons par présenter les fonctionnelles de Mumford--Shah et d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli et le principe de l'approximation champ de phase. Ensuite, en dimension $1$, nous établissons la convergence des points critiques dans le cas où l'on rajoute à la fonctionnelle d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli une condition d'obstacle. En dimension quelconque, la convergence des points critiques est connue sous l'hypothèse supplémentaire que l'énergie d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli converge. En dimension $2$, nous montrons ce résultat en ne supposant qu'une partie de la convergence de l'énergie. Enfin, nous étudions le système parabolique associé aux équations vérifiées par les points critiques d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli. Nous établissons l'existence, les conditions d'unicité et la régularité des solutions de ce système, et obtenons en particulier leur régularité maximale en toute dimension.

Je présenterai notamment de nouvelles méthodologies pour contrôler les fausses découvertes grâce à des bornes de confiance et des procédures de contrôle du False Discovery Rate (FDR). Ces procédures assurent un recouvrement post hoc, ce qui signifie qu'elles préservent les garanties statistiques même après l'intervention du praticien --- comme le p-hacking ou le HARKing --- et offrent une plus grande flexibilité en lui permettant de sélectionner l'ensemble de rejets de manière adaptative. De plus, ces méthodes exploitent également la structure des données ; elles vont au-delà de l'hypothèse i.i.d. traditionnelle en prenant en compte l'hétérogénéité des données afin d'améliorer la puissance statistique.

rec.title: Scattering and smoothing for the two-dimensional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
rec.speaker: Muyuan Lyu
rec.abstract:
Scattering theory describes the large-time behavior of nonlinear evolution equations through comparison with a linear flow. This raises a further question: can the nonlinear correction to the asymptotic state be smoother than the initial data?
I will begin with an introduction to scattering for nonlinear Schrödinger equations, highlighting several developments that motivate this question. I will then present a deterministic smoothing result for the two-dimensional cubic equation. Assuming that a solution scatters in the harmonic Sobolev space (\mathcal H^s), with (s>0), the difference between its scattering state and its initial datum belongs to (\mathcal H^{s+\sigma}) for every (0<\sigma<\min{2s,1}). The proof combines the lens transform, which turns the large-time problem into a finite-time endpoint problem, with bilinear Strichartz estimates and harmonic spectral analysis. The emphasis will be on the mechanism behind the regularity gain. The talk is intended for graduate students in analysis, with no prior familiarity with nonlinear scattering required.

rec.title: Anti-classification results in dynamical systems
rec.speaker: Matthew Foreman
rec.abstract:
Thematic 3-weeks programme at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris, May 18th to June 4th, 2027.
Beware: It was reported to us that scammers are sending to participants fraudulent e-mails about accommodation/fees. Please be particularly cautious about e-mails not coming from the organisers nor from an @ihp.fr address.
REGISTRATION IS FREE, HOWEVER MANDATORY.
Presentation of the programme
In recent years, there have been major advances using techniques from Descriptive Set Theory to show, in a rigorous way, that many classical problems in Dynamical Systems are impossible to solve. In this context, a problem that can be set in a Polish space is said to be impossible to solve if it cannot be settled using inherently countable techniques. These groundbreaking results mostly lie in Ergodic Theory, with further significant advances in Topological and Smooth Dynamical Systems.
One main goal of this program is to further enhance interactions between Descriptive Set Theory and Dynamical Systems. It brings together researchers from different fields to settle some of the most famous problems in dynamics dating to the mid-20th century.
A second main goal is to expand applications of the techniques from Descriptive Set Theory to other areas of mathematics.
Week 1
The program begins with lectures introducing the basic impossibility techniques and lectures explaining fundamental concepts in areas of potential applications.
We plan to have tutorials on:
Impossibility Results
Ergodic Theory
Symbolic Dynamics
Smooth Dynamical Systems
Additionally, there will be Research Talks and Expository Lectures (primarily in Ergodic Theory and Descriptive Set Theory).
Week 2
Research talks in Descriptive Set Theory, Ergodic Theory, Smooth and Symbolic Dynamics, as well as Expository Lectures, including on:
Impossibility Results in Ergodic theory
Complexity Theory
Flexibility and Rigidity
Moreover, we will have Problem and Discussion Sessions.
Week 3
Topical Days (particularly Complex Dynamics with tutorial); Problem Sessions

rec.abstract:
Thematic trimester programme with short courses, seminars and workshops
September 14th to December 4th, 2026 at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris
REGISTRATION IS FREE AND MANDATORY
Click here to register for the trimester
IMPORTANT WARNING: Scam / Phishing / SMiShing! Note that ill-intentioned people may be trying to contact some of participants by email or phone to get money and personal details, by pretending to be part of the staff of the conference center. IHP and the organisers will NEVER contact you by phone on this issue and will NEVER ask you to pay for accommodation / board / possible registration fee in advance.
Deadline for financial support request is March 15, 2026
Operator algebras are self-adjoint subalgebras of the bounded operators on a Hilbert space and divide into two main classes: C∗-algebras and von Neumann algebras, according to whether one demands that they are closed in the norm topology or the weak operator topology. When one first meets these algebras, they might look quite similar, but they have different natures as exemplified by the commutative case: via the Gelfand transform, abelian C∗-algebras are algebras of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on a locally compact Hausdorff space, while abelian von Neumann algebras are essentially bounded measurable functions on a measure space. These flavours persist in general. Topological concepts such as dimension and invariants such as K-theory pervade the study of C∗-algebras, while measure-theoretic style methods are often used to study von Neumann algebras.
The long thematic program OA will focus on operator algebras and its still evolving interactions with ergodic theory, topological dynamics, discrete subgroups of semisimple Lie groups, analytic, ergodic and geometric group theory, quantum information theory and random matrices.

rec.abstract:
This is a thematic trimester programme with short courses, seminars and workshops on Kinetic theory: from long-range interactions to turbulence and quantum simulators.
January 18 to April 9, 2027 at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris
REGISTRATION IS MANDATORY AND FREE
IMPORTANT WARNING: Scam / Phishing / SMiShing! Note that ill-intentioned people may be trying to contact some of participants by email or phone to get money and personal details, by pretending to be part of the staff of the conference center. IHP and the organizers will NEVER contact you by phone on this issue and will NEVER ask you to pay for accommodation/ board / possible registration fee in advance.
Deadline for financial support request has been extended to: June 30th, 2026.
Summary
The program centers on the development of a unified understanding of kinetic theory in systems with long‑range interactions, with a particular emphasis on the quantum regime. Long‑range interacting quantum systems—realized experimentally in cold atoms, trapped ions, and polar molecules—exhibit rich dynamical behavior such as metastability, collisionless dynamics, anomalous transport, critical scaling, and turbulence‑like phenomena. These effects are often linked to the Vlasov equation, the collisionless kinetic equation that emerges in the thermodynamic limit. While Vlasov theory is conceptually well established in classical plasma physics, its systematic extension to quantum many‑body systems remains incomplete.
A key scientific motivation of the program is that different communities—mathematical physics, quantum many‑body theory, and AMO physics—address similar non‑equilibrium long‑range phenomena using different methods, preventing the emergence of a unified framework. The program aims to bridge these approaches and clarify conceptual connections between classical and quantum kinetic theories.
The scientific agenda spans several interconnected themes. One major theme is the analysis of classical transport, Vlasov dynamics, and their differences from Boltzmann kinetic theory, including how turbulence, chaos, and long‑range correlations emerge in classical systems. Another theme concerns the quantum generalizations of Vlasov theory, focusing on rigorous derivations and effective equations for quantum gases, including mean‑field and Gross–Pitaevskii limits, and the treatment of finite‑size effects in quantum simulators.
The program will explore non‑equilibrium many‑body dynamics in quantum systems, including quantum turbulence, cascade processes, ergodicity breaking, and anomalous scaling. A related line of inquiry concerns the dynamics of quantum correlations and entanglement, the onset of quantum chaos, and the characterization of universal quasi‑static dynamics in isolated systems. Another scientific direction is the study of effective theories in quantum matter, connecting renormalisation‑group methods with kinetic descriptions and identifying the regimes where classical scaling concepts can illuminate quantum behavior.
On the mathematical side, the program emphasizes rigorous derivations of macroscopic equations from microscopic many‑body dynamics, particularly in long‑range systems, and the formulation of effective transport equations, scaling limits, and mean‑field theories. Renormalisation‑group tools are highlighted both in their rigorous and approximate forms, with the aim of connecting microscopic models to emergent large‑scale behavior in many‑body systems.
Finally, the proposal identifies a scientific need to synthesize current insights into a coherent and predictive quantum kinetic theory for long‑range interactions, and to outline a roadmap of open problems invol

March 1 to 5, 2027 - IHP, Paris
Summary
This workshop aims to synthesize established paradigms from classical transport with the overlapping frameworks of quantum dynamics, forging a coherent pathway toward understanding transport phenomena, turbulence, and chaos in strongly correlated quantum matter. Of central observable importance is the interferometric comparison between the mean-field Vlasov description and the collisionally decohered Boltzmann equation—highlighting the nonlocal phase-space structures endemic to long-range interacting systems, in stark contrast with the short-range statistical closures of local theories.

Recent trends at the interface between information theory, probability, statistics and high-dimensional geometry raise new questions on the role and importance of entropy in the understanding of both asymptotic and finite range phenomena, in particular towards discrete structures and applications to areas such as quantum information, percolation and random matrices. Recent fruitful developments warrant imminent blossom of new ideas and results in this area in the near future.
Another central theme at the interface of High-Dimensional Probability and Convexity is the study of isoperimetric properties of log-concave measures (including isoperimetric-type questions related to convex bodies). This is not a mere curiosity: convexity and isoperimetry play an important role in the study of concentration of measure phenomena which is crucial for harnessing various high-dimensional effects in Probability as well as several applied fields.
The scope of the semester includes developing further connections between Information Theory and Convexity, in all of the different directions described above. The semester will aim to strengthen these powerful interdisciplinary methods, aiming towards challenging issues and applications, including the isoperimetry questions for log-concave measures, and super-concentration properties of models from random matrix theory and statistical mechanics.
The semester’s objective is to foster cross-fertilization between probability, analysis, information theory and convex geometry (continuous and discrete). By organizing two thematic pre-schools, we will ensure active participation by junior researchers, which should have a lasting effect on their careers, as well as influence the routes along which these research areas will be developed in the future. Our two workshops will further provide opportunities for many re- searchers from across the globe to interact and collaborate. We believe that close interactions between these disciplines are a necessary condition to address many mathematical challenges raised in the last decades, and that the timing is optimal to bring together all these powerful ideas which have been recently developed in several communities. Therefore, our proposed semester program will have a strong and lasting impact on High-Dimensional Probability, Convexity and Analysis as a whole.

Presentation of the programme
Quantum cryptography lies at the intersection of cryptography, quantum information, and computational complexity. Quantum technologies offer new cryptographic possibilities, while also changing our understanding of which security guarantees and computational tasks are achievable. Recent developments have revealed deep connections between these areas, but many fundamental questions remain open.
This programme will bring together researchers from theoretical computer science, mathematics, cryptography, and quantum information. It will explore three closely connected directions: information-theoretic foundations, including quantum communication, nonlocality, randomness, and device-independent security; complexity-theoretic foundations, including quantum proofs, verification, reductions, and computational assumptions; and computational and interactive primitives, including commitments, zero knowledge, secure computation, and protocols involving quantum devices.
Through an introductory school, seminars, focused workshops, informal discussions, and extended research visits, the programme aims to develop a common language across neighboring communities. It will provide opportunities for sustained collaboration between senior and junior researchers, encourage new research partnerships, and help identify important directions for the next stage of quantum cryptography.

rec.title: Séminaire 09/10/2026 - Gabriel Peyré and Vianney Perchet
rec.abstract:
14h15-15h15 Gabriel Peyré (ENS)
The Expressive Power of Large Language Models
Abstract: Large language models process vast sequences of input tokens by alternating between classical multi-layer perceptron layers and self-attention mechanisms. While the approximation capabilities of perceptrons are relatively well understood, those of attention mechanisms remain less explored. In this talk, I will compare the proof techniques and approximation results associated with these two types of layers, emphasizing key open questions that connect large language models with approximation theory in infinite-dimensional spaces representing input token distributions.
15h30-16h30 Vianney Perchet (Criteo et ENSAE)
AI-powered AI. Robustness, Consistency and Smoothness of Algorithms.
Abstract: AI systems no longer operate as isolated algorithms, machines, or agents; instead, they
interact with each other. An algorithm designed for a specific task might use the output or
prediction of another as its input. This has serious consequences: blindly relying on another
algorithm can be extremely helpful if it is accurate, but devastating if it is not, as a single error -
even the tiniest one - could break down the whole system. New algorithms will need to incorporate
these predictions to improve their consistency, while remaining robust against errors. We will use
simple toy examples to show how the generic framework of learning-augmented algorithms (LAA) is
perfectly suited for this challenge, highlighting the complexity of designing practical and potentially
vastly more efficient algorithms.
