arxiv:2610.22299.summary: How many disjoint copies of some graph $H$ can appear in an induced subgraph of a strongly regular graph? We give upper and lower bounds that depend on the number of vertices in their boundary. This generalizes a result of Lou-Murin which bounds the independence number of a (hitherto still elusive) strongly regular graph with parameters $(99,14,1,2)$.

arxiv:2610.22305.title: $h$-cobordisms between $1$-connected manifolds with boundary
arxiv:2610.22305.summary: We classify $h$-cobordisms between compact simply-connected $4$-manifolds with boundary in both the smooth and topological categories. This extends a result of Kreck, which proved the corresponding result for closed manifolds. As an application, we recover the injectivity portion of Orson-Powell's computation of the mapping class group for simply-connected topological $4$-manifolds with boundary.

arxiv:2610.22326.title: Stratification of opers with apparent singularities and isomonodromic bubbling
arxiv:2610.22326.summary: On a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$, we study Simpson's stratification of the de Rham moduli space of rank-2 flat connections. Upon representing flat $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$-connections by branched projective structures, or equivalently by opers with apparent singularities, the stratum containing a flat connection is determined by the minimal number of apparent singularities needed to represent it. We construct explicit holomorphic families in which two simple apparent singularities collide and disappear, so that the family crosses into a smaller stratum; this realizes Simpson's closure relation between strata near generic points.
arxiv:2610.22326.authors: Duong Dinh, Troy Figiel, Joerg Teschner

arxiv:2610.22359.title: Integral and higher-genus quantum McKay correspondence in type D
arxiv:2610.22359.summary: We establish Iritani's integral form of the $\mathbb{C}^\times$-equivariant Crepant Transformation Conjecture (CTC) for the minimal resolution of the surface singularity $\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$, where $\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$ is the binary dihedral group of order $4n$. We then use Givental's quantisation formalism to prove the all-genus full-descendent CTC in that case. As an application, we deduce the Bryan-Cadman-Young degree-zero form of the orbifold Gromov-Witten/Donaldson-Thomas correspondence for the Calabi-Yau 3-orbifold $[\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}] \times \mathbb{C}$.

arxiv:2610.22388.title: Eventual Exactness and Rigidity for Abelian Covers of Groups
arxiv:2610.22388.summary: For a group $G$, let $a(G)$ denote the minimum number of abelian subgroups covering $G$, and let $\omega(G)$ be the maximum size of a pairwise noncommuting set. We prove the exact formula $\sup_{\omega(G)\leq n}a(G)=2^{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}+1$ for every $n\geq 63$. Equality holds precisely for groups with derived subgroup of order two and binary symplectic central quotient of dimension $2\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$.

arxiv:2610.22410.title: The square achievement game on $n \times n$ boards
arxiv:2610.22410.summary: Two players alternately claim cells of an $n \times n$ grid; the first to hold all four corners of an axis-parallel square wins, and a full board without one is a draw. The first player has a winning strategy if and only if $n \ge 5$, which answers a question of Erickson. For $n \ge 6$ one strategy serves every board: a rule with no lookup table whose moves after the second reply are all forcing, built around the plus, a stone with the four cells at a common distance from it along the axes, a shape proposed for this game by Sirgedas in 2010.

arxiv:2610.22493.title: Generating functions of hypermaps and m-constellations with two alternating boundaries
arxiv:2610.22493.summary: We study the enumeration of planar hypermaps with several alternating boundaries. We first derive a peeling recursion with an arbitrary number of alternating boundaries and, in the two- boundary case, translate it into a functional equation for the corresponding generating function. Our main result is an explicit solution of this equation for m-constellations.

arxiv:2610.22494.title: Presentability of categories of localizations and analytic rings
arxiv:2610.22494.summary: We prove that certain categories of Bousfield localizations are presentable and give explicit regular cardinals $\kappa$ for which they are $\kappa$-presentable. As an application, we show that the category of analytic rings in the sense of Clausen and Scholze is $(2^{\aleph_0})^+$-presentable.
arxiv:2610.22494.authors: Wern Juin Gabriel Ong, Gabriel Ribeiro

arxiv:2610.22495.title: Asymptotic dimension of graphs excluding an induced or fat minor
arxiv:2610.22495.summary: Asymptotic dimension is a large-scale invariant of metric spaces that was introduced by Gromov (1993). A major open problem in coarse graph theory asks whether, for every fixed graph $H$, the class of graphs excluding $H$ as a fat minor has bounded asymptotic dimension. A weaker conjecture asserts the same conclusion for graphs excluding $H$ as an induced minor.
arxiv:2610.22495.authors: Robert Hickingbotham, Freddie Illingworth, Piotr Micek, Bartosz Walczak

arxiv:2610.22559.title: Four colours are needed for closed-neighbourhood conflict-free colouring of all planar graphs
arxiv:2610.22559.summary: A colouring of the vertices of a graph is conflict-free with respect to closed neighbourhoods if every closed neighbourhood contains a colour that appears on exactly one of its vertices. The colouring need not be proper. Every planar graph has such a colouring with four colours.

arxiv:2610.22571.title: Quantum Periods from TBA and Continued Fractions
arxiv:2610.22571.summary: We consider quantum A-periods of local ${\mathbb P}^1 \times {\mathbb P}^1$, or equivalently the generating function of constant terms for powers of the Laurent polynomial $x + x^{-1} + y + y^{-1}$ where $x$ and $y$ are $q$-commuting variables. We derive a number of new representations for these rich combinatorial and algebraic objects. First, we find that the well-known TBA equation encodes not only the A-period itself but also higher diagonal modes of the corresponding noncommutative Laurent polynomials.
arxiv:2610.22571.authors: Alexander Chervov, Ilia Gaiur, Sergey Galkin, Fedor Levkovich-Maslyuk, Volodya Rubtsov, Shamil Shakirov

arxiv:2610.22573.title: Computing S(X) for Ruled Surfaces Defined by Stable Bundles on Curves of Genus 2
arxiv:2610.22573.summary: This paper discusses the algebra of symmetric tensors for ruled surfaces defined by rank 2 stable vector bundles on curves of genus 2. The algebra is computed for special bundles $E$ when $S^2 E$ is destabilized by a line bundle and when $S^3 E$ is destabilized by a bundle of rank 2. A strategy for computation is discussed in regards to the other special bundles $E$.

arxiv:2610.22582.title: The Schubert bialgebra
arxiv:2610.22582.summary: We introduce a Schubert bialgebra $\mathcal{A}=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, in which polynomials in different numbers of variables multiply to zero and the coproduct splits the variables into two consecutive blocks, and study its graded dual $\mathcal{D}$, whose product is concatenation of weak compositions. The Schubert polynomials $\mathfrak{S}_u^n$ form a basis of $\mathcal{A}$; we give an explicit formula for the dual Schubert basis $\Xi_u^n$ of $\mathcal{D}$ via a transition formula to an elementary symmetric basis, and show that the Schubert structure constants $c_{u,v}^w$ are the coefficients of the coproduct of $\mathcal{D}$ in the dual Schubert basis. The product…

arxiv:2610.22620.title: Complete regular dessins: the nonmetacyclic case
arxiv:2610.22620.summary: We classify regular dessins on $K_{2^e,2^f}$ with nonmetacyclic colour-preserving automorphism group, retaining the two specified vertex rotations. We give nonredundant presentations and exact counts in both the abelian and nonabelian Frattini cases. For orientation- and colour-preserving isomorphisms, the number is $2^{2e-2}+16$ when $e=f\ge4$ and $3\cdot2^{2f-3}+16$ when $e>f\ge4$, with explicit counts for all smaller exponents.

arxiv:2610.22622.title: Axis-parallel square packing with an exact formula for optimal packing of seven squares
arxiv:2610.22622.summary: How large a square is needed to hold axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths? We give exact formulas for the optimal side through seven squares, with explicit constructions and geometric lower-bound proofs. For every $n\ge6$, the optimum for $n$ squares is a sum of at most $n-3$ of the prescribed side lengths.

arxiv:2610.22644.title: A holomorphic motion with non-subharmonic Hausdorff dimension
arxiv:2610.22644.summary: We present an example of a holomorphic motion of a Cantor set $\lambda \mapsto A_\lambda$ for which neither the Hausdorff dimension $\dimH(A_\lambda)$ nor the lower Minkowski dimension $\dimMl(A_\lambda)$ is a subharmonic function of~$\lambda$. This answers negatively a question of Fuhrer--Ransford--Younsi, and distinguishes these dimensions from packing and upper Minkowski dimensions, for which subharmonicity holds. All four dimensions are computed explicitly.

arxiv:2610.22651.title: A $\mathbb{C}$-motivic $w_1$-self-map of periodicity 1
arxiv:2610.22651.summary: Let $\mathrm{DY} = \mathbb{1}/(\eta, \nu) \in \mathrm{SH}(\mathbb{C})$. We construct a $w_1$-self-map of periodicity 1 $w:\Sigma^{5,3}\mathrm{DY} \to \mathrm{DY}.$ The cofiber is a realization of $DA(1)$, the double of the subalgebra $A(1)$ of the $\mathbb{C}$-motivic Steenrod algebra $A$.

arxiv:2610.22654.title: Absolute continuity of invariant measures for random diffeomorphisms
arxiv:2610.22654.summary: We develop criteria showing that invariant measures for random walks generated by diffeomorphisms of manifolds are in the Lebesgue class. Our assumptions are first, that there is a uniform expansion gap in the Lyapunov spectrum of the random walk, and second, that the conditionals of the invariant measure along the appropriate (partial) stable manifolds are in the Lebesgue class.
arxiv:2610.22654.authors: Aaron Brown, Alex Eskin, Simion Filip, Federico Rodriguez Hertz

arxiv:2610.22658.title: Singular vectors of sparse random rectangular matrices: Transition between delocalized and semilocalized phases
arxiv:2610.22658.summary: Consider the bipartite Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graph $\mathbb{G}(n,m,d/\sqrt{mn})$ at the critical sparsity $d = b\log(N)$ for some $b > 0$ with $N = n + m$, and constant aspect ratio $\gamma = n/m \geq 1$. We show that the spectrum of its centered and rescaled bi-adjacency matrix, whose limiting law is the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur (MP) distribution, is split into two phases: in the bulk, singular vectors are completely delocalized, while near the edges, singular vectors are semilocalized, with their mass concentrating on small disjoint balls, centered at vertices with extreme degrees. As $b$ decreases, we identify sharp thresholds for the emergence of outlier singular values.

arxiv:2610.22663.title: Rational decomposition of polyhedra and a conjecture of Brlek and Reutenauer
arxiv:2610.22663.summary: We prove in the affirmative a conjecture of Brlek and Reutenauer (2003), which relates unambiguous rational sets to a well known result due to Khovanskii and Pukhlikov (1992) and independently to Lawrence (1990) on the valuations of the algebra spanned by the indicator functions of polyhedra.

arxiv:2610.22669.title: String functions and cyclotomic Hecke algebras
arxiv:2610.22669.summary: In this paper we study the Kleshchev multipartitions that label simple modules of certain cyclotomic Hecke algebras with parameters $1$ and $-1$. The $2$-residue statistic divides these multipartitions into blocks. We deduce a bivariate generating function for the blocks using representation theory.
arxiv:2610.22669.authors: Dennis Stanton, Ting Xue, Ae Ja Yee

arxiv:2610.22678.title: Generic vanishing for Dolbeault cohomology of mixed Hodge modules on abelian varieties
arxiv:2610.22678.summary: We study generic vanishing for the Dolbeault cohomology of mixed Hodge modules, where the differentials in the Dolbeault complex are modified by a one-form. We prove that, on the Dolbeault moduli space of Higgs line bundles, the cohomology support loci of mixed Hodge modules agree with the images of the cohomology support loci of their underlying $\mathscr{D}$-modules on the de Rham moduli space under the map induced by the nonabelian Hodge correspondence. We further apply this result to study Fourier-Mukai transforms of mixed Hodge modules on abelian varieties.

arxiv:2610.22679.title: Vector bundles on singular surfaces and threefolds
arxiv:2610.22679.summary: We fully classify vector bundles of critical rank on normal affine surfaces and threefolds over algebraically closed fields via their Chern classes. We also prove existence of rank $2$ bundles on threefolds with prescribed first and second motivic Chern classes. The main input is the motivic filtration on algebraic $K$-theory: its third piece is generated by smooth closed points and is identified with motivic cohomology by the third Chern class.

arxiv:2610.22696.title: On exponential stability of generalized linear functional differential equations
arxiv:2610.22696.summary: We develop a general approach to uniform exponential stability for a broad class of linear functional differential equations with Volterra operators. The considered class includes delay differential equations, integro-differential equations, equations with distributed delays, vector equations, and systems of scalar functional differential equations. Standard assumptions on the equation are relaxed to include measurable parameters.

arxiv:2610.22730.title: Hypercube Richardson varieties from magic words
arxiv:2610.22730.summary: Inspired by the recent preprint of Ellenberg, Libedinsky, Plaza, Simental, and Williamson, we study the geometry of Richardson varieties whose associated Bruhat intervals are boolean posets. We define magic words for a Bruhat interval and prove that for intervals with magic words the associated Richardson variety is a tower of $\mathbb{P}^1$-s. We also prove that the Bruhat intervals consisting of the dyadically well-distributed permutations all have magic words.

arxiv:2610.22755.title: $a$-numbers of covers in characteristic two: semigroups and Riemann-Roch spaces
arxiv:2610.22755.summary: We compute the $a$-numbers of the Garcia-G\"uneri-Stichtenoth curves, the Beelen-Montanucci curves, and the Skabelund covers of Suzuki curves in characteristic two. The proofs use the identity $a(X)=\ell(\tfrac12\operatorname{div}(dt))$ and reduce the calculations to Riemann-Roch spaces on the base curves. We obtain transfer formulas for odd-degree radical covers, with one or several points at infinity, and evaluate them using Weierstrass semigroups and plane sections of the Hermitian curve.
arxiv:2610.22755.authors: Gilberto B. Almeida Filho, Saeed Tafazolian, St\'efani C. Vieira

arxiv:2610.22758.title: $R$-trivial Galois cohomology classes and cohomological $p$-dimension
arxiv:2610.22758.summary: Given a prime $p$, a field $F$ of characteristic different from $p$ and a finite $p$-primary Galois module $V$, a Galois cohomology class in $H^n(F,V)$ is called $R$-trivial if it can be connected to $0$ by a class defined over an open subscheme of the projective line. All classes of $H^n(F,V)$ are $R$-trivial if $F$ has cohomological $p$-dimension at most $n$, by the Bloch-Kato conjecture. We show that this bound is sharp: working over fields of iterated Laurent series, we produce, for every $n\geq 1$, a field $F$ of cohomological $p$-dimension $n+1$ and a Galois module $V$ such that $H^n(F,V)$ contains classes which are not $R$-trivial.

arxiv:2610.22772.title: Semialgebraic ${C^m}$ solutions to a univariate system of linear inequalities with Nash forcing
arxiv:2610.22772.summary: Let $(A_{ij}(x))_{1 \leq i \leq N, 1 \leq j \leq M}$ be a matrix of univariate semialgebraic functions. We study the solvability of the system of linear inequalities \begin{equation*} \sum_{j=1}^M A_{ij}(x)F_j(x)\leq f_i(x) \ \ \text{ for } i = 1, \ldots, N, \end{equation*} where we assume each forcing $f_i$ is a Nash function. We show that the $C^m$ solvability of the system can be characterized by finitely many linear ordinary differential inequalities in $f$ with semialgebraic coefficients depending only on $(A_{ij})$.

arxiv:2610.22773.title: Spectral asymmetry and odd cycles in integral graphs
arxiv:2610.22773.summary: We prove that the triangle $C_3$ is the only integral unicyclic graph with an odd cycle. The main tool is a spectral inequality that does not require integrality: if $G$ is a connected non-bipartite graph and $G-e$ is bipartite for some edge $e$, then the eigenvalues $\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n$ of $G$ satisfy $\sum_{i}(\lambda_i+\lambda_{n+1-i})^+\le 2$ and $0<\lambda_1+\lambda_n\le 1$. It follows from comparing $A(G)$ with the signed adjacency matrix obtained by reversing the sign of $e$, which is similar to $-A(G)$, through a common rank-one perturbation and Weyl's monotonicity theorem.
arxiv:2610.22773.authors: Rodrigo O. Braga, Jean Carlo Moraes, Matheus C. Santos

arxiv:2610.22774.title: The Involution Rank of $\MCG(\Sigma_3)$ Is Four
arxiv:2610.22774.summary: For the closed orientable surface $\Sigma_3$, we prove \[ \irank\MCG(\Sigma_3)=4.\] Thus $\MCG(\Sigma_3)$ can be generated by four involutions, but not by three. This settles the genus-three case of Farb's problem on generation by involutions.

arxiv:2610.22775.title: On the existence of mixed orthogonal arrays of strength two with six factors
arxiv:2610.22775.summary: Orthogonal arrays are foundational objects in combinatorial design theory and experimental design theory, with broad applications in computer science, coding theory, and cryptography. In this paper, we investigate the existence for mixed orthogonal arrays of strength two with six factors, and propose several new constructions based on incomplete orthogonal Latin squares, incomplete transversal designs, and $\Sigma$-resolvable transversal designs. As a result, we show that the necessary conditions for the existence of such mixed orthogonal arrays are also sufficient, except for a small number of known exceptions and nine unsettled cases.
arxiv:2610.22775.authors: Xiuling Shan, Guangzhou Chen, Xiangrong Sun

arxiv:2610.22783.title: Counterexamples to the local antimagic leaf conjecture
arxiv:2610.22783.summary: It has been conjectured that $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T)\leq\ell(T)+2$ for every tree $T$ of order at least three, where $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T)$ is the local antimagic chromatic number and $\ell(T)$ denotes the number of leaves. We disprove this bound and show that no absolute constant can replace $2$ in an inequality of this form. Our approach uses degree-based intervals containing all possible induced vertex weights under bijective edge labelings, together with a separation criterion that forces selected internal vertex weights to be distinct.
arxiv:2610.22783.authors: Andr\'e Ebling Brondani, Francisca Andrea Macedo Fran\c{c}a

arxiv:2610.22808.title: Complete characterization of disconnected one-point unions of cycles with local antimagic chromatic number 2
arxiv:2610.22808.summary: A graph $G = (V, E)$ that admits a bijective edge labeling $f:E \to\{1,\ldots ,|E|\}$ is local antimagic if $f$ induces a vertex labeling $f^+$ such that for any pair of adjacent vertices $x$ and $y$, $f^+(x)\not= f^+(y)$, where the induced vertex label $f^+(x)= \sum f(xu)$, with $u$ ranging over all the vertices adjacent to $x$. The minimum number of distinct induced vertex labels over all local antimagic labelings of $G$ is the local antimagic chromatic number of $G$, denoted $\chi_{la}(G)$. In this paper, we completely characterize all the disconnected one-point unions of cycles (having at most 3 components) with local antimagic chromatic number 2.

arxiv:2610.22809.title: Low-weight compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal M_{g,n}^{ct}$ and the extended Torelli morphism
arxiv:2610.22809.summary: We study the weight zero and weight two graded pieces of the compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal M_{g,n}^{ct}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus $g$ of compact type and show that they are computed by bridgeless graph complexes. In weight two, we construct a natural embedding of shifted weight zero cohomology from lower genus. For unmarked curves, we construct canonical classes represented by pinched odd wheel graphs and prove that distinct wheel monomials give linearly independent classes in the dual of $W_0H_c^{2g}(\mathcal M_g^{ct};\mathbb Q)$.

arxiv:2610.22829.title: KKM meets colorful Carath\'eodory
arxiv:2610.22829.summary: The colorful Carath\'eodory theorem states that if $V_1,\dots,V_{d+1}\subset\mathbb R^d$ satisfy $0\in\mathrm{conv}\;V_i$ for every $i$, then there exist points $v_i\in V_i$ such that $0\in\mathrm{conv}\;\{v_1,\dots,v_{d+1}\}$. We give a new proof based on triangulations and the classical KKM lemma. We lift the sets $V_i$ to parallel affine copies of $\mathbb R^d$ in $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d$ and use a triangulation of the resulting point configuration to construct a KKM cover.

arxiv:2610.22838.title: The Spectral Theory of Threshold Graphs: A Survey
arxiv:2610.22838.summary: Threshold graphs-the $\{P_4, C_4, 2K_2\}$-free graphs, equivalently those built from a single vertex by repeatedly adding isolated or dominating vertices-are among the most thoroughly studied graph classes in spectral graph theory. This survey collects results on the spectrum of threshold graphs across the full range of matrices studied in the literature: the adjacency, Laplacian, and signless Laplacian matrices; the distance, distance Laplacian, and distance signless Laplacian matrices; the eccentricity and Seidel matrices; and the normalized adjacency, Laplacian matrix-together with the associated graph energies, cospectrality questions, extremal spectral radius problems, and several…
arxiv:2610.22838.authors: Pallabi Manna, Santanu Mandal, Fernando C. Tura

arxiv:2610.22849.title: Marchal-type lemmas for the restricted $(N+1)$-body problem with their applications
arxiv:2610.22849.summary: The direct methods of calculus of variations have had a great success in the classical Newtonian $N$-body problem in this century. First in finding periodic solutions and more recently in the existence of parabolic, hyperbolic and hyperbolic-parabolic solutions. The foundation of many of these results is Marchal's lemma, which guarantee's fixed-end local minimizers are collision-free and hence classical solutions of the $N$-body problem.

arxiv:2610.22857.title: Separable elements and Bruhat orders
arxiv:2610.22857.summary: We prove the curious fact that, in any Coxeter group, the intersection of a principal left weak order ideal $[e,x]_L$ with a principal right weak order ideal $[e,y]_R$ has a unique maximal element $\mathrm{lr}(x,y)$ under Bruhat order. We apply this to resolve a conjecture of Hart and Rowley on involutions in weak order ideals. This fact arises from, and is applied to, our study of the theory of separable elements in finite Weyl groups.

arxiv:2610.22870.title: Continuity of biaccessibility dimension for polynomials
arxiv:2610.22870.summary: For a polynomial $f$ of degree $d\geq 2$, its biaccessible set $B(f)$ consists of angles whose external rays are smooth and land at a point receiving at least two smooth external rays. We prove that the function $f\mapsto {\rm dim}_H(B(f))$ is continuous on the entire space of degree-$d$ polynomials. Therefore $(\log d){\rm dim}_H (B(f))$ gives a continuous extension of classical core entropy from the postcritically finite case to all polynomials of degree $d$.

arxiv:2610.22875.title: Overtake and the recursive-line equality for second-order Zarankiewicz numbers
arxiv:2610.22875.summary: We study two questions about the second-order Zarankiewicz numbers. The first is the recursive-line equality $z_2(m,n)=z_{RL}(m,n)$, known to hold in every computed case and conjectured in general. The second, here called \emph{overtake}, is the strict inequality $z_{2A}(m,n)>z_2(m,n)$ between the second-order augmented number and the second-order number.

arxiv:2610.22902.title: Triangle-free Rank--Ramsey graphs from ordered incidence lifts
arxiv:2610.22902.summary: For a graph $G$ with adjacency matrix $A_G$ and a coefficient field $\mathbb K$, put $\rho_{\mathbb K}(G)=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb K}(A_G+I)$. We answer the triangle-free Rank--Ramsey existence question of Beniamini, Linial and Shraibman. For every order $n$, we construct a triangle-free graph $H_n$ such that, simultaneously over all coefficient fields, $$ \rho_{\mathbb K}(H_n)=\bigl(4(2/3)^{3/4}+o(1)\bigr)n^{3/4}, $$ with an error uniform in the field.
arxiv:2610.22902.authors: Yong Lu, Qi Wu, Qiannan Zhou

arxiv:2610.22909.title: Sharp Bounds for Common Spanning Forests under Color Refinement
arxiv:2610.22909.summary: We study the common spanning structure of connected finite simple graphs that are indistinguishable by uniformly initialized color refinement. We prove that any two such graphs with common cyclomatic number $r\ge2$ contain isomorphic spanning forests with at most $r-1$ components. This bound depends only on $r$ and is sharp for every $r\ge2$.

arxiv:2610.22916.title: Signed dual graphs and face spectral gaps of Cayley 2-complexes
arxiv:2610.22916.summary: We construct a weighted signed dual multigraph for the Cayley $2$-complex of a finite presentation and represent its $\ell^2$ face Laplacian as a signed graph Laplacian with a diagonal potential. We prove that the face spectral gap above the kernel vanishes for the Baumslag--Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(1,m)$, $m\ge2$, using explicit finitely supported face chains. Our main vanishing theorem gives the same conclusion for every finitely presented amenable group with ordinary first Betti number at least two.
arxiv:2610.22916.authors: Bobo Hua, Yong Lin, Tao Wang, Haohang Zhang

arxiv:2610.22920.title: Bounded Leaf Volumes and Analytic Quotients of Singular Holomorphic Foliations
arxiv:2610.22920.summary: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a singular holomorphic foliation of dimension $k$ on a compact K\"ahler manifold $M$ of dimension $n$. Suppose that the volumes of its regular leaves are uniformly bounded, $\dim(Sing\mathcal{F})<k$, and the union of the leaf closures meeting $Sing\mathcal{F}$ has finite $2k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. We prove that the quotient by chains of intersecting leaf closures is a normal compact complex analytic space of dimension $n-k$.

arxiv:2610.22926.title: Approximation and extension theorems for normal affine toric varieties
arxiv:2610.22926.summary: We study approximation and extension problems for holomorphic maps from Stein spaces to normal affine toric varieties, continuing the work of L\"ark\"ang and L\'arusson. Normality allows us to obtain twisted factorizations for arbitrary holomorphic maps from factorial complex spaces, including degenerate maps. This yields approximation and extension theorems under weaker cohomological assumptions.

arxiv:2610.22938.title: Enumeration of small vertex-transitive directed strongly regular graphs
arxiv:2610.22938.summary: We find the 728 vertex-transitive directed strongly regular graphs with parameters $(v,k,t,\lambda,\mu)$ where $1 \le v \le 39$ and $k < v/2$ and $0 < t < k$. A table with parameters and automorphism groups and some additional data is given.

arxiv:2610.22967.title: An Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa theorem for induced packings of even cycles
arxiv:2610.22967.summary: We show that for every graph $G$ and every positive integer $k$, $G$ contains either $k$ vertex-disjoint even cycles with no edges between distinct cycles, or a set of $O(k^2\log k)$ vertices whose closed neighborhood meets every even cycle of $G$. Moreover, we give a polynomial-time algorithm that outputs one of the two outcomes. As an application, we show that every $K_{1,t}$-free graph containing no induced packing of $k$ even cycles has tree-independence number $O(tk^2\log k)$, with a corresponding decomposition computable in polynomial time.
arxiv:2610.22967.authors: Jungho Ahn, Lars Jaffke, O-joung Kwon, Paloma T. de Lima, Hyemi Park

arxiv:2610.22971.title: Sharp asymptotics for the Lov\'asz number of random circulant graphs
arxiv:2610.22971.summary: We study the LOV\'ASZ number of dense random circulant graphs generated by independent Bernoulli bits indexed by cyclic distances. Although only $O(n)$ independent random inputs determine $O(n^2)$ globally dependent edge indicators, we prove sharp expectation asymptotics along all odd orders, including composite orders, with leading constant one. This resolves a conjecture posed for random circulant graphs in 2025.
arxiv:2610.22971.authors: Xin Chen, Hongwei Hu, Yanqing Hu, Wei Wang, Luzhen Yang

arxiv:2610.22986.title: Rigorous verification of period-doubling bifurcations in maps
arxiv:2610.22986.summary: We present a computer-assisted approach for proving period-doubling bifurcations in one-parameter families of maps $x \mapsto f(x,\lambda)$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We solve a square augmented system, called the period-doubling map, whose unknowns are the fixed point, the parameter, the right eigenvector attached to the eigenvalue $-1$, the left eigenvector with its eigenvalue, and the vector which describes the center manifold to second order. A contraction argument gives a solution close to a numerical approximation, at which the Jacobian is invertible.

arxiv:2610.22993.title: Hypergraphs of Low Degree Without Independent Transversals
arxiv:2610.22993.summary: For every fixed $k\ge 3$ and every integer $b\ge 2$, we construct a finite vertex-partitioned $k$-uniform hypergraph with blocks of size $b$ and no independent transversal. We show that the maximum number of edges meeting a block is $\left(\frac{(k-1)^{k-1}}{k^k}+O_k(b^{-1})\right)b^k,$ while the maximum vertex degree is $\left(\frac{(k-2)^{k-2}}{(k-1)^{k-1}}+O_k(b^{-1})\right)b^{k-1}$. This shows that the known bound on the number of edges meeting a block is asymptotically sharp even when the leading constant in the maximum vertex degree tends to zero, which answers a problem of Groenland, Kaiser, Treffers, and Wales.

arxiv:2610.23003.title: Perron-Wright asymptotics and critical component processes for regular inhomogeneous random graphs
arxiv:2610.23003.summary: We extend Wright's enumeration of connected labelled graphs with fixed surplus to irreducible critical finite type kernels and regular compact type kernels. Let $C_t(k,r)$ denote the total weight of connected labelled graphs with $k$ vertices and surplus $r$. Let $u>0$ satisfy $Ku=u$ and $\int u\,d\mu=1$, and put $\alpha=\int u^2\,d\mu$ and $\beta=\int u^3\,d\mu$.

arxiv:2610.23004.title: A cubulation of the associahedron using a torus-equivariant degeneration of the brick variety
arxiv:2610.23004.summary: We describe a mixed subdivision of the $(n-1)$-dimensional Loday associahedron into $(n-1)!$ maximal cells which are combinatorial cubes, and we show that the face poset of this subdivision is isomorphic to the face poset of the subdivision of the $1\times 2\times \dotsb \times (n-1)$ box into unit cubes. More generally, we describe mixed subdivisions of generalized associahedra into pieces which are Minkowski sums of Bruhat interval polytopes. Our subdivisions arise from a torus-equivariant embedded (in a product of flag varieties) degeneration of brick varieties into reduced unions of products of Richardson varieties.

arxiv:2610.23024.title: The geometric exceptional set for Fano threefolds
arxiv:2610.23024.summary: We study the geometric exceptional set in Manin's conjecture for smooth Fano threefolds. We prove that every adjoint rigid surface with $a$-invariant one on a non-product smooth Fano threefold is normal. This yields a description of the geometric exceptional set in terms of the higher-$a$ locus, anticanonical conics, and del Pezzo fibrations.

arxiv:2610.23055.title: Typical representations of admissible type I algebraic supergroups
arxiv:2610.23055.summary: We study typical representations of an admissible type I algebraic supergroup $G$. We prove that, for a dominant weight $\lambda$, the induced supermodule $H^0_G(\lambda)$ is simple if and only if $\lambda$ is typical and the induced module $H^0_{G_{\mathrm{ev}}}(\lambda)$ for the even subgroup $G_{\mathrm{ev}}$ is simple. We establish equivalences between typical blocks for $G$ and blocks for $G_{\mathrm{ev}}$, and give a projectivity criterion for Kac modules over every Frobenius kernel.

arxiv:2610.23058.title: A note on the non-wandering dynamics in the $n$-fold symmetric products
arxiv:2610.23058.summary: We construct a homeomorphism on a compact metric space whose non-wandering set consists of a single fixed point, while the induced map $F_n(f)$ possesses infinitely many (non-fixed) non-wandering points.

arxiv:2610.23059.title: Counterexamples to Two Conjectures on Tangles in Matroid Minors
arxiv:2610.23059.summary: We give counterexamples to two conjectures of Brettell, Jowett, Oxley, Semple, and Whittle concerning tangles in matroid minors. We construct a matroid $P_0$ with a tangle $\mathcal T$ of order seven. For each $i\in\{4,5,6,7\}$, let $\mathcal T_i$ denote its order-$i$ truncation.

arxiv:2610.23100.title: Comparing word probabilities in finite groups
arxiv:2610.23100.summary: We use results from extremal graph theory and analysis to compare word probabilities in finite groups. In particular, we show that the probability of satisfying the 2-Engel word admits a positive lower bound in terms of the probability that an element has order dividing 3. More generally, using a group removal lemma, we obtain analogous bounds for $x^m$-good words.

arxiv:2610.23152.title: Minimal asymptotic \(g\)-adic bases from arbitrary partitions
arxiv:2610.23152.summary: Let $g>h\ge2$ be integers. For a nonempty set $W\subseteq\N$, let $\mathcal F^*(W)$ denote the set of its finite nonempty subsets. Let $$A_g(W)=\left\{\sum_{f\in F}a_fg^f: 1\leq a_f \leq g-1,F \in \mathcal F^*(W)\right\},$$ and let $\N=W_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup W_h$ be a partition into infinite sets.

arxiv:2610.23159.title: Generalization of Navascu\'es' $\alpha$-fractal operator on lifted Sierpi\'nski gasket
arxiv:2610.23159.summary: The primary objective of the present article is to extend Navascu\'es' class of $\alpha$-fractal interpolation functions ($\alpha$-FIFs) from a Euclidean domain to a non-Euclidean domain. Precisely, we consider the lifted Sierpi\'nski gasket $\big(\widetilde{SG}\big)$, which is a subset of the first Heisenberg group equipped with a \textit{non-Euclidean metric} (popularly known as the Heisenberg metric), and demonstrate the existence of the class of $\alpha$-FIFs in the continuous space on $\widetilde{SG}$. Subsequently, we derive certain conditions on the parameters so that the same class lies in the H\"{o}lder space on $\widetilde{SG}$.
arxiv:2610.23159.authors: Gurubachan, S. Verma, V. V. M. S. Chandramouli

arxiv:2610.23164.title: Rational torus equivariant spectra VII: the Cousin complex
arxiv:2610.23164.summary: We explore the analogy between rational G-spectra for an r-torus G and sheaves over an r-dimensional scheme, in the context of the author's algebraic model for rational G-spectra. In particular, the resolution of the sphere of a virtual representation in the standard model corresponds precisely to the Cousin complex resolution of a line bundle. The tom Dieck splitting for the sphere of an actual respresentation corresponds to the collapse of the Cousin spectral sequence by degrees, and the the non collapse in other cases corresponds to familiar geometric behaviour.

arxiv:2610.23171.title: Point Modules of Non-Connected Graded Algebras
arxiv:2610.23171.summary: As part of a program to extend the homogeneous coordinate ring techniques of Artin-Tate-Van den Bergh to twisted graded Calabi-Yau (tCY) algebras, we initiate the study of point modules of non-connected graded algebras. We define weak and strong point modules of graded quotients of path algebras and compute their respective moduli stacks. We describe the relation between these point stacks and the classical point schemes in the connected graded setting, and we analyze the point stacks of several 2 and 3-dimensional tCY algebras.

arxiv:2610.23180.title: Critical cusp cancellation and analytic response for a Bernoulli random interval map
arxiv:2610.23180.summary: We show that the critical cusp exponent $\beta=-1/2$ admits $W^{2,1}$ invariant densities in an explicit family of expanding full-branch interval maps. The usual estimates exclude this exponent because two zero-order coefficients in the second derivative of the transfer operator are individually non-integrable. Their signed combination, however, contains the factor $\beta(2\beta+1)$ for a pure power cusp.

arxiv:2610.23209.title: Regular Additive Scalar Invariants of ${\mathcal N}=1$ Hyperbolic Spin Supertriangles
arxiv:2610.23209.summary: We classify regular cyclic scalar invariants of non-degenerate hyperbolic ${\mathcal N}=1$ spin supertriangles which are additive under geodesic subdivision. After fixing the spin lift, the common-first gauge (introduced in earlier work by the second-named author and further developed here) gives a complete $3|4$ modulus of such supertriangles.. The space of additive scalar invariants is proved to have superdimension $3|1$: ordinary hyperbolic area in degree zero, two even generators in degree two, and one odd generator in degree three; the degree-one and degree-four sectors vanish.

arxiv:2610.23215.title: The Smith-Toda complex V(4) exists for p >= 11
arxiv:2610.23215.summary: We show that the Smith-Toda complex V(4) exists for all primes p >= 11. This improves on the recently announced result by OpenAI that V(4) exists at the prime 1009.

arxiv:2610.23224.title: Regularity, depth and Serre depth of symbolic powers of complementary edge ideals
arxiv:2610.23224.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $I_c(G)$ denote its complementary edge ideal. In this paper, we study the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity, the depth and Serre depth for $(S_{2})$ of the symbolic powers of $I_c(G)$. We derive explicit formulas for $\operatorname{reg} I_c(G)^{(k)}$ and $\operatorname{reg} I_c(G)^{(k)}/I_c(G)^k$ for every $k\geq1$, in terms of the number and the sizes of the connected components of $G$.
arxiv:2610.23224.authors: Antonino Ficarra, Somayeh Moradi, Yuji Muta

arxiv:2610.23227.title: Seven ordered points and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
arxiv:2610.23227.summary: We prove that the ordered GIT quotient of seven points on $\mathbb P^1$ with equal weights is not isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of any arithmetic complex ball quotient. Together with our companion paper and the known positive examples, this determines the equal weight case for every $n\ge6$: such a realization exists precisely for $n=6,8$. The lattice and the algebraic isomorphism are unrestricted, and torsion and divisorial ramification are allowed.
arxiv:2610.23227.authors: Ryunosuke Nakano (Hokkaido University), Hisato Matsukawa (Hokkaido University)

arxiv:2610.23228.title: Weighted configurations and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
arxiv:2610.23228.summary: We prove that, for every $n\ge9$, no ordered GIT quotient of $n$ points on $\mathbb P^1$ with positive rational weights smaller than one and of total weight two is isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of an arithmetic complex ball quotient. The weights may lie on stability walls, and the lattice may have torsion and ramify along divisors. No compatibility with a prescribed period map is assumed.
arxiv:2610.23228.authors: Ryunosuke Nakano (Hokkaido University), Hisato Matsukawa (Hokkaido University)

arxiv:2610.23236.title: On the complexification of $ q $-deformations of compact semisimple Lie groups
arxiv:2610.23236.summary: For the quantised algebra of functions on a simply connected compact semisimple Lie group, we study the relationship between the primitive spectrum, topologically irreducible representations by bounded operators on Hilbert spaces, and quantum holomorphic evaluations induced via the Drinfeld double. In terms of the Joseph stratification of the primitive spectrum, we prove a sharp dichotomy: primitive ideals in homogeneous strata always arise as kernels of topologically irreducible representations by bounded operators on a Hilbert space, whereas those in inhomogeneous strata do not admit any such realisations. We further show that, unlike in the classical situation, quantum holomorphic…

arxiv:2610.23270.title: A Generalized Half-Singleton Bound for List Decoding of Insertion/Deletion Errors
arxiv:2610.23270.summary: We derive an upper bound on the rate of a linear code capable of list decoding from insertion and deletion errors. Subsequently, we show that a linear code can list decode from at most $n - \frac{L}{L+1}k + 1$ insdel errors with fixed list size $L$, and that this bound is strict when the code does not contain the all-ones vector. We also provide a simple construction of codes achieving the optimal rate for any given list size capable of correcting a single insdel error.
arxiv:2610.23270.authors: Neehar Verma, Camilla Hollanti, Razane Tajeddine

arxiv:2610.23278.title: The Compactness Theorem for Enriched Logic
arxiv:2610.23278.summary: The framework of enriched logic extends positive logic (also known as coherent logic) from sets to structures internal to a symmetric monoidal closed category $\mathcal{V}$. This framework was developed by Rosick\'y and the second-named author. The main novelty of this logic is that the arities of the function and relation symbols are now objects in $\mathcal{V}$.

arxiv:2610.23295.title: Orthogonal Projections and Assouad Dimension: Resolving Fraser's Questions
arxiv:2610.23295.summary: We examine two questions on exceptional orthogonal projections for Assouad dimension. Let $1\le k<d$ and $1\le q<d$. For a set $F$ contained in a $q$-dimensional subspace $W\subset\R^d$ and containing a nonempty relatively open subset of $W$, we compute both the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of the exceptional $k$-planes as $k(d-k)-|q-k|-1$.

arxiv:2610.23312.title: The Strong Total Cover Problem
arxiv:2610.23312.summary: The Strong Total Cover Problem (STCP) is a novel covering problem defined on a graph $G = (V, E)$, where the objective is to find a minimum-cardinality subset $T \subseteq V \cup E$ such that every element of $V \cup E$ is covered. In this setting, a vertex covers itself and all its incident edges, while an edge covers itself together with its two endpoints. The STCP resembles classical covering problems such as Vertex Cover and Edge Cover problems, and naturally arises as the dual of the total matching problem.

arxiv:2610.23320.title: Folding to the Bessel-Clifford system, and Equivariant Topological Recursion
arxiv:2610.23320.summary: We study the interplay between symmetry reductions of meromorphic connections, folding, and topological recursion. As a motivating example, we realize the Bessel-Clifford system as a folding of a symmetry-invariant subspace of the $0-$member of the Painlev\'e IV hierarchy. We introduce equivariant topological recursion for spectral curves with a Klein four-group $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry and prove that the corresponding equivariant correlators can be folded to the ordinary topological recursion correlators on the quotient spectral curve.

arxiv:2610.23321.title: Anomalies for compact simple Lie groups via $G$-kernels for loop group nets
arxiv:2610.23321.summary: Let $G$ be a compact simply connected simple Lie group and $k \geq 1$. Jump loops give an outer homomorphism $\theta_k$ from $G$ to the outer automorphisms of the local factor of the level-$k$ loop group net, which is the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor. We show that its Sutherland obstruction is $k$ times the positive basic class in $H^3_{\mathrm{Borel}}(G, \mathbb{T}) \cong H^{4}(BG, \mathbb{Z})$ and that $\theta_k$ is faithful, so it is a $G$-kernel.

arxiv:2610.23329.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of six bodies for all positive masses: Part I, exceptional-mass first limits
arxiv:2610.23329.summary: We separate the generic positive-mass finiteness problem for planar six-body central configurations from finiteness on exceptional mass loci. The Chang--Chen diagram enumeration has 117 graphs. The arguments below confine 40 first-limit diagram obligations to proper necessary mass loci.

arxiv:2610.23376.title: Ambient Chow Rings of Debarre--Voisin Fourfolds and the Beauville--Voisin Conjecture
arxiv:2610.23376.summary: We prove the Beauville--Voisin conjecture for a very general Debarre--Voisin hyperk\"ahler fourfold \(Y\subset\Gr(6,10)\) associated with a trivector \(\sigma\) on a ten-dimensional complex vector space \(V_{10}\). Namely, the cycle class map is injective on the subalgebra of the Chow ring generated by divisor classes and the Chern classes of the tangent bundle.

arxiv:2610.23399.title: A Generating Polynomial for Convex Subsets of Posets
arxiv:2610.23399.summary: For any finite poset we define a generating polynomial counting upsets, downsets, and their intersection. We investigate the behaviour of this polynomial with respect to poset operations and show that it distinguishes certain posets constructed with the operations of ordinal sum and disjoint union, including Series-Parallel posets as a special case. Lastly, we comment on connections to the causal set approach to quantum gravity.

arxiv:2610.23417.title: Entropy estimates and volume rigidity for graphs with positive Bakry-\'Emery curvature
arxiv:2610.23417.summary: We establish a volume bound for weighted graphs with positive Bakry--\'Emery curvature through entropy estimates for the heat flow and characterize the equality case. As a consequence, if a connected unweighted graph $G=(V,E)$ satisfies the Bakry--\'Emery curvature--dimension condition $CD(2,\infty)$ with respect to the unnormalized Laplacian, then $$ |V|\le 2^d, $$ where $d$ denotes the maximum degree. Equality holds if and only if $G$ is a hypercube.
arxiv:2610.23417.authors: Yanlong Ding, Shiping Liu, Chiyu Zhou

arxiv:2610.23430.title: Brauer-Manin obstruction for symmetric powers
arxiv:2610.23430.summary: For a quasi-projective smooth geometrically integral variety $X$ over a number field, we prove that the Brauer-Manin obstruction for its symmetric powers coincides with the obstruction coming from $X$. As a consequence, Brauer-Manin obstruction for the symmetric powers cannot provide new cohomological obstruction to weak approximation of zero-cycles for $X$. The key intermediate ingredients are a Dold-Thom type result for Brauer groups and a precise descent formula for adelic points.

arxiv:2610.23457.title: Smooth Limits of Stable Manifolds
arxiv:2610.23457.summary: Let X be a compact complex manifold of dimension n, and suppose that X is deformation equivalent to a stable manifold. Then X is projective whenever n <=3. We also construct, for every n >=4, smooth families of compact complex manifolds over the unit disc such that every fiber over the punctured disc is a stable manifold, while the central fiber is a non-Kahler Moishezon manifold.

arxiv:2610.23471.title: Odd Cycle Decompositions
arxiv:2610.23471.summary: We determine the asymptotic minimum-degree threshold for decompositions into cycles of every fixed odd length. We prove that, for each odd integer $\ell\ge3$, every $\eps>0$ and sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $C_\ell$-divisible graph $G$ with minimum degree $\delta(G)\ge (\ell/(2\ell-2)+\eps)n$ has a $C_\ell$-decomposition, where $C_{\ell}$ denotes the cycle of length $\ell$. The constant is best possible.
arxiv:2610.23471.authors: Jianfeng Hou, Caiyun Hu, Hezhi Wang

arxiv:2610.23478.title: Subvariety intervals and limit varieties of zero extensions of mirror-word semirings
arxiv:2610.23478.summary: For the mirror word $\mathbf{m}_n=a_1\cdots a_na_n\cdots a_1$, let $\mathcal{V}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n))$ and $\mathcal{W}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n)^0)$. We show that $[\mathcal{W}_n,\mathcal{W}_{n+1}]$ ($n\geq 1$) and $[\mathcal{V}_n,\mathcal{W}_n]$ ($n\geq 2$) have cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Every variety in $[\mathcal{W}_2,\mathcal{W}_\infty]$ has infinite axiomatic rank.

arxiv:2610.23485.title: Lefschetz Pencils on surfaces and an application to Seshadri constants
arxiv:2610.23485.summary: Let $X$ be a nonsingular complex projective surface and let $L$ be a very ample line bundle on $X$. We study the question: when does a general pencil in the linear system $|L|$ consist of only irreducible and reduced curves? We give a precise condition which guarantees an affirmative answer: in fact, this holds if and only if the genus of a general member of $|L|$ exceeds the irregularity of $X$.

arxiv:2610.23487.title: Small and large quasi-kernels: a weighted transfer theorem
arxiv:2610.23487.summary: A quasi-kernel of a digraph $D$ is an independent set from which every vertex is reachable by a directed path of length at most two. The Small Quasi-kernel Conjecture asserts that every source-free digraph on $n$ vertices has a quasi-kernel of size at most $n/2$, whereas the Large Quasi-kernel Conjecture asks for a quasi-kernel whose closed out-neighbourhood has size at least $n/2$. Spiro proved that the former implies the latter.
arxiv:2610.23487.authors: Jiangdong Ai, Gregory Gutin, Xiangzhou Liu, Xianhao Meng

arxiv:2610.23505.title: mixed Hodge structures on the strictly upper triangular Lie algebras
arxiv:2610.23505.summary: We show that, for $k\geq 3$, a lattice in the unitriangular Lie group $U_k(\mathbb{R})$ is the fundamental group of a smooth quasi-projective complex algebraic variety if and only if $k=3$. The proof uses the conjugation symmetry and weight conditions of mixed Hodge structure on the Malcev Lie algebra proven by Morgan. This result identifies a family of groups that must be excluded in the search for smooth quasi-projective varieties with torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups of high nilpotency class.

arxiv:2610.23516.title: On the crystalline Artin--Mumford invariant
arxiv:2610.23516.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ and let $W=W(k)$. We prove that the torsion subgroup of $H^3_{\mathrm{cris}}(X/W)$ is a birational invariant of smooth projective varieties over $k$. The proof combines the action of correspondences on Hodge--Witt cohomology and on the first Nygaard piece of the de Rham--Witt complex.

arxiv:2610.23553.title: Visibility Sets, Empty Pentagons, and Sufficient Conditions for Hexagons
arxiv:2610.23553.summary: Given a set $S$ of $n$ points in general position in the plane, we define the $C$-set $C(p,q)$ of an oriented edge $(p,q)$ as the set of extreme points of the visibility set $V(p,q)$ facing $(p,q)$. Since every point of $V(p,q)$ that is not in $C(p,q)$ gives rise to an empty convex pentagon having $(p,q)$ as a boundary edge, it is natural to study the properties of $C$-sets in order to bound the number of empty convex pentagons of $S$. We prove tight bounds on the intersection size and union complexity of $C$-sets sharing an endpoint.

arxiv:2610.23572.title: Phases in the cyclic quantum dilogarithm: correction to "Cyclic quantum Teichm\"uller theory"
arxiv:2610.23572.summary: We first correct $\boldsymbol{\mu}_N$-phase issues in the basic definition around the cyclic quantum dilogarithm operators in [Ish26]. In particular, the notion of global coefficients must be extended by incorporating additional lifting data forming a $\boldsymbol{\mu}_N$-cover, and the pentagon relation generally acquires an extra $\boldsymbol{\mu}_N$-factor. Nevertheless, we prove that every point in a regular locus of the partially compactified cluster Poisson variety lifts to a \emph{strict} extended global coefficient, for which this extra $\boldsymbol{\mu}_N$-factor is trivial.

arxiv:2610.23594.title: Arithmeticity, superrigidity, and totally geodesic submanifolds of infinite-volume hyperbolic manifolds
arxiv:2610.23594.summary: Given an infinite-volume convex cocompact hyperbolic manifold with Fuchsian ends and infinitely many maximal properly immersed totally geodesic submanifolds of dimension at least two intersecting its convex core, we show that it (infinitely) covers an arithmetic hyperbolic manifold. This answers the general version of a question of Oh. As a byproduct of our techniques, we also give a Ratner-type classification of $\mathrm{SO}_0(m,1)$-invariant Radon measures whose support intersects the frame bundle of the interior of the convex core.

arxiv:2610.23626.title: Four New Single-Error-Correcting Binary Codes
arxiv:2610.23626.summary: We construct a $(16, 3072, 3)$-code, a $(17,6144,3)$-code, an $(18,12288,3)$-code and a $(19,24576,3)$-code. Consequently, we get four new lower bounds: $A(16,3) \geq 3072$, $A(17,3) \geq 6144$, $A(18,3) \geq 12288$ and $A(19,3) \geq~24576$. Each of the codes consists of a union of cosets of a linear code.

arxiv:2610.23633.title: On the Length of Maximum Sum-Rank Distance Codes
arxiv:2610.23633.summary: The classical theory of arcs in finite projective spaces provides a powerful geometric framework for studying maximum distance separable (MDS) codes and their possible lengths. In this paper, we investigate how this perspective extends to maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD) codes, whose geometric description involves systems of linear sets rather than individual projective points. Our main goal is to understand how the block structure of an MSRD code constrains its length.

arxiv:2610.23637.title: Two-generator presentations with a relation gap
arxiv:2610.23637.summary: We exhibit two-generator two-relator group presentations that have cyclic relation modules but do not present one-relator groups; this resolves the relation gap problem. By attaching a single 3-cell to each of the corresponding presentation 2-complexes, one obtains counterexamples to Wall's D2 problem.
arxiv:2610.23637.authors: Laurent Bartholdi, Martin R. Bridson, Roman Mikhailov, John Nicholson

arxiv:2610.23644.title: A Topological Quantum Field Theory for Representation Varieties of Torus Links
arxiv:2610.23644.summary: We construct a Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT) that computes the virtual classes of $G$-representation varieties associated with the fundamental group of a torus link complement. Following the framework established by Gonz\'alez-Prieto, Logares and Mu\~noz for $G$-representation varieties of surface groups, we introduce a suitable bordism whose iteration enables a recursive topological evaluation of these virtual classes. Via this TQFT, we explicitly compute the virtual class of these varieties for the groups $G=\mathrm{AGL}_1(\mathbb{C})$ and $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$.

arxiv:2610.23664.title: Line spreads of W(2n-1, q), q even
arxiv:2610.23664.summary: Let q be an even prime power and n \ge 2. We construct line spreads of the symplectic polar space W(2n-1,q) by replacing pairwise disjoint reguli in a Desarguesian line spread. The construction is based on partitions of the points of PG(n-1,q^2) into points of a nondegenerate Hermitian variety and Baer sublines meeting that variety in exactly one point.
arxiv:2610.23664.authors: Daniele Bartoli, Antonio Cossidente, Giuseppe Marino, Francesco Pavese

arxiv:2610.23672.title: Homology and carrier faces of simplicial distributions
arxiv:2610.23672.summary: We study the facial structure of simplicial distribution polytopes using topological and algebraic methods. In the theory of simplicial distributions, measurement and event spaces are represented by simplicial sets, and compatible probability assignments form a convex polytope. Given a simplicial distribution, it is known that its supports determine its carrier face.

arxiv:2610.23684.title: The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
arxiv:2610.23684.summary: Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points.

arxiv:2610.23689.title: Local topological zeta functions of generic symmetric and catalecticant determinantal varieties
arxiv:2610.23689.summary: We give explicit formulas for the local topological zeta functions at the origin of generic symmetric determinantal varieties and catalecticant determinantal varieties associated with generic Hankel matrices. In the symmetric determinant hypersurface case, the formula simplifies to a closed product expression and implies the Strong Monodromy Conjecture. For catalecticant determinantal varieties, we establish a simultaneous local reduction of the determinantal ideals and obtain a closed product formula for their local topological zeta functions.

arxiv:2610.23711.title: Finite Cyclic Fundamental Groups and Exotic Universal Covers from the Cartwright--Steger Surface
arxiv:2610.23711.summary: We use a particular nodal curve on the Cartwright-Steger surface to construct minimal symplectic four-manifolds with arbitrary nontrivial finite cyclic fundamental group and fixed topological invariants $(e,\sigma,\chi_h,c_1^2)=(43,1,11,89)$. Using these symplectic four-manifolds as building blocks, we construct a symplectic 4-manifold that is homeomorphic to $(22m-1)\mathbb{CP}^2\#(21m-1)\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}$ for any integer $m\geq 2$.
arxiv:2610.23711.authors: Anar Akhmedov, B. Doug Park, S\"{u}meyra Sakall{\i}, Sai-Kee Yeung

arxiv:2610.23712.title: Involutions on $(\infty,n)$-categories of bordisms and reflection TQFTs
arxiv:2610.23712.summary: We construct a strict involution, that is, a strict $\mathbb{Z}/2$-action, on the $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathbf{Bord}_n(H_n)$ of bordisms with $H_n$-structure, where $H_n$ is the symmetry type of a TQFT, using the complete $n$-fold Segal space model. Using this involution, we develop an appropriate definition of reflection TQFTs in this setting and show that they correspond to certain homotopy fixed point spaces. Finally, we apply the machinery to the example of super algebras, where, depending on the symmetry type, the homotopy fixed point data corresponds to either a stellar structure or a real structure on the algebra that the reflection theory assigns to the point.

arxiv:2610.23719.title: Confluence relations, Hoffman basis over \mathbb{Z}_{(2)}, and the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
arxiv:2610.23719.summary: We express every admissible word as a $\mathbb{Z}_{(2)}$-linear combination of Hoffman words and explicit confluence relations. This implies that every multiple zeta value is a linear combination of elements of the Hoffman basis with coefficients having odd denominators, as conjectured by Hirose and Sato. Combined with Brown's theorem and Furusho's characterization of the Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller group $\mathrm{GRT}$ by confluence relations, our result identifies the de Rham motivic Galois group of mixed Tate motives over $\mathbb{Z}$ with $\mathrm{GRT}$ and gives an alternative proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture, for which a proof was previously presented in the OpenAI Math…

arxiv:2610.23731.title: Two-bridge knot epimorphisms and intersections in the character variety
arxiv:2610.23731.summary: We study the SL(2,C) character varieties of hyperbolic two-bridge knot groups admitting epimorphisms onto the trefoil knot group. Ohtsuki, Riley, and Sakuma give a systematic construction of an infinite family of such knots. The character varieties of these knot groups contain a component of irreducible representations arising from the epimorphism, which is distinct from the canonical component.
arxiv:2610.23731.authors: Isidora Bailly-Hall, Michelle Chu, Karina Dovgodko, Akash Ganguly, Jiachen Kang, Jishi Sun

arxiv:2610.23752.title: Spectral networks, finite webs, and the $T_3$ cubic differential
arxiv:2610.23752.summary: We describe spectral networks for cubic differentials on $\mathbf{P}^1$ with exactly three poles all of order two, following observations of Hollands-Neitzke. To do so, we give a precise definition and establish some basic properties of a class of finite webs (corresponding to BPS states in physics) in the cubic differential setting, including their non-vanishing central charge. Turning to the example, we prove that at rational angles the network is totally degenerate; the number of walls and Stokes regions is explicitly computed and depends on an arithmetic criterion.

arxiv:2610.23755.title: The maximum number of Hamiltonian cycles in tournaments
arxiv:2610.23755.summary: Let $C(n)$ denote the maximum number of directed Hamiltonian cycles in a tournament on $n$ vertices. We prove that, as $n\to\infty$, $$ C(n) = \left(\frac{\cosh 1}{\cos 1}\pm o(1)\right)\frac{(n-1)!}{2^n}. $$ The bound is asymptotically attained by the regular tournament with vertices $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ where $(i,j)$ is a directed edge if $j - i \pmod n< n/2$.

arxiv:2610.23758.title: Operations on $G$-sets and the Dress map
arxiv:2610.23758.summary: We study versions of binomial and multichoose coefficients for finite $G$-sets, extending a result of Siebeneicher from the 1970s concerning the duality between these operations. If the group $G$ comes from a finite Galois extension of fields, the Dress map provides a bridge from $G$-sets to quadratic forms over the base field. We show that this Dress map is compatible with binomial coefficients of finite $G$-sets and a particular operation on quadratic forms we define.

arxiv:2610.23778.title: Dg models for derived differential operators
arxiv:2610.23778.summary: We show that for any algebra $R$ that is essentially of finite type over a field $k$, the derived functors of Smith-Van den Bergh admit a dg enhancement. In particular, for any $R$-module $M$ one can associate a dg algebra of differential operators $E_M$ whose cohomology is a nilpotent thickening of the (classical) ring of $k$-linear differential operators on $M$. We show that these dg algebras fit into a framework of Koszul duality due to Dwyer-Greenlees and specializes to a derived ring of differential operators studied by Yang when $M=R$ and $k=\mathbb{C}$.
arxiv:2610.23778.authors: Jack Jeffries, Devlin Mallory, Claudia Miller, Josh Pollitz, Eamon Quinlan-Gallego

arxiv:2610.23790.title: Near optimal gap in the Lonely Runner Conjecture
arxiv:2610.23790.summary: For a set $V$ of $n$ distinct positive integers, let $\mathrm{ML}(V)=\max_{t\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\min_{v\in V}\|vt\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. We prove that there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that for every $n\ge2$ and every $V$, \[ \mathrm{ML}(V)>\frac{1+c}{2n}. \] The proof combines a refinement of the large GCD argument of Green and Walker with a new physical spillover inequality for interval multiplicities.

arxiv:2610.23792.title: Revisiting separators in string graphs, region intersection graphs, and induced-minor-free graphs
arxiv:2610.23792.summary: String graphs are intersection graphs of continuous curves in the plane. In 2010, Fox and Pach proved that string graphs with $m$ edges admit balanced vertex separators of size $\mathcal{O}(m^{3/4}\sqrt{\log m})$ and conjectured that this bound can be improved to $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m})$, which would be optimal. After partial progress, Lee claimed in 2017 to prove this conjecture, and more generally to prove analogous separator theorems for region intersection graphs over minor-closed graph families.
arxiv:2610.23792.authors: James Davies, Pawe{\l} Rz\k{a}\.zewski, Jack Spalding-Jamieson, Bartosz Walczak

arxiv:2610.23794.title: Symplectic Lie groups and nilmanifolds associated with acyclic quivers
arxiv:2610.23794.summary: We give combinatorial criteria for the existence of left-invariant symplectic forms on the positive and full path Lie groups of finite acyclic quivers. For the nilpotent positive path Lie groups, the criterion also determines whether their compact quotients admit symplectic forms and forces the nilpotency step to be at most three. For the completely solvable full path Lie groups, we give a direct combinatorial criterion and an equivalent recursive criterion.

arxiv:2610.23803.title: Deligne--Faltings Logarithmic Derived Geometry with a View towards Logarithmic GLSM
arxiv:2610.23803.summary: Many perfect obstruction theories and virtual cycles in enumerative geometry are shadows from derived geometry. In this paper, we give a general construction of reduced perfect obstruction theories arising from a geometric reduction of the derived stack $X$ with respect to a $(-1)$-shifted log function $w_\alpha$. Notably, this construction leads to a decomposition of the virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ into the reduced virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{red}}$ and a reduced boundary cycle $[\Delta_X]^\red$.

arxiv:2610.23816.title: Twisted $\mathbb{A}^1$-degrees of Wronski maps
arxiv:2610.23816.summary: The Wronski map is a central object of study in osculating Schubert calculus, and has been the focus of much work in real algebraic geometry over the last few decades due to its remarkable reality properties. In this work, we study it over arbitrary fields through the lens of quadratically-enriched enumerative geometry. A basic obstruction is that the Wronski map is not oriented in general, so existing approaches do not apply directly.

arxiv:2610.23838.title: A stable multipersistence invariant for ladder modules
arxiv:2610.23838.summary: We define an additive functor S that assigns a three parameter persistence module to every morphism between one parameter persistence modules. We show that if the morphism is bar-to-bar, then its image under S is rectangle decomposable. We prove that S is stable with respect to the interleaving distance and study further properties of the functor related to rectangle decompositions.
arxiv:2610.23838.authors: Marco Delgado-Garrido, Lars Moberg Salbu, Alvaro Torras-Casas, Rocio Gonzalez-Diaz

arxiv:2610.23846.title: Identifiability from Moments in Independent Component Analysis Mixture Models
arxiv:2610.23846.summary: We study Independent Component Analysis (ICA) mixture models. These models consist of mixtures of ICA densities. An ICA density is associated with a random vector whose coordinates become mutually independent after an invertible linear transformation.
arxiv:2610.23846.authors: Pardis Semnani, Konstantin Usevich, Elina Robeva

arxiv:2610.23855.title: Unitary $S^1$-Manifolds with Four Fixed Points and Kosniowski's Conjecture
arxiv:2610.23855.summary: We study unitary \(S^1\)-manifolds with four isolated fixed points in relation to Kosniowski's conjectural inequality \(4\chi(M)>\dim M\). For every integer \(m\ge3\), we show that there exists a unitary \(S^1\)-manifold \(M_m^{18}\) with exactly four isolated fixed points, and these manifolds are pairwise distinct and nonzero in ordinary complex bordism. Since \(\chi(M_m^{18})=4\), they give an infinite family of counterexamples to \(4\chi(M)>\dim M\).
arxiv:2610.23855.authors: Zhi L\"u, Jun Ma, Qiangbo Tan

arxiv:2610.23920.title: Almost Empty Monochromatic Polygons in Planar Point Sets
arxiv:2610.23920.summary: For integers $r \ge 3$, $c \ge 2$, and $s \ge 0$, let $\mathsf{M}_r^{\star}(c,s)$ denote the smallest integer such that any set of at least $\mathsf{M}_r^{\star}(c,s)$ points in the plane in general position (no three on a line), colored with $c$ colors, contains a monochromatic $r$-gon (not necessarily convex) with at most $s$ interior points. Define $\lambda_r^{\star}(c)$ to be the smallest integer such that $\mathsf{M}_r^{\star}(c,\lambda_r^{\star}(c)) < \infty$. The case of triangles, that is, $r=3$, has been studied in recent years.
arxiv:2610.23920.authors: Bhaswar B. Bhattacharya, Sandip Das, Sk Samim Islam, Aashirwad Mohapatra, Saumya Sen

arxiv:2610.23958.title: Unranking $S$-avoiding permutations with two forbidden offsets
arxiv:2610.23958.summary: Given a finite family of combinatorial objects with a total order, ranking asks for the position of a given object, and unranking asks for the object occupying a given position. Both provide algorithmic access to families too large to enumerate. Kagey gave a polynomial-time algorithm for several position-restricted families and left open the case of $\{-1,1\}$-avoiding permutations.

arxiv:2610.23965.title: Two characterizations of chain partitioned probe graphs
arxiv:2610.23965.summary: Chain graphs are exactly bipartite graphs without induced $2K_2$ (a graph with four vertices and two disjoint edges). A graph $G=(V,E)$ with a given independent set $S\subseteq V$ (a set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices) is said to be a chain partitioned probe graph if $G$ can be extended to a chain graph by adding edges between certain vertices in $S$. %there exists a set $E'\subseteq\binom{S}{2}$ such that the graph $G'=(V,E\cup E')$ is a chain graph. In this note we give two characterizations for chain partitioned probe graphs.

arxiv:2610.23989.title: Planar Disk Filters and Real Chromatic Roots at Beraha Numbers
arxiv:2610.23989.summary: We construct simple plane triangulations whose chromatic polynomials have real roots accumulating at every noninteger Beraha number $B_\ell=4\cos^2(\pi/\ell)$; the integer values $0,1,2,3$ are roots of $K_4$. The construction rests on the observation that a triangulated disk with four boundary vertices acts, inside a larger triangulation, as a transfer operator lying in a commutative three-parameter algebra. Rotating such disks by a quarter turn and composing them in series moves their eigenvalue triples around this algebra in a controllable way, and for every fixed $q\in(B_{10},4)$ one can manufacture a finite disk whose two competing local eigenvalues are strictly dominated by the third…

arxiv:2610.23991.title: Gaps for PLRS with zero coefficients
arxiv:2610.23991.summary: Zeckendorf proved that every positive integer has a unique decomposition as a sum of non-adjacent Fibonacci numbers. Among its extensions, we focus on Positive Linear Recurrence Sequences (PLRS): fixed depth recurrences with non-negative integral coefficients whose first and last terms are positive: $G_{n+1} = c_1 G_n + \dots + c_L G_{n-L+1}$ with $c_i$ non-negative integers and $c_1 c_L \ge 1$. We again find every integer can be written uniquely as an appropriate sum of terms of the sequence, and we can study the distribution of gaps between summands in decompositions.
arxiv:2610.23991.authors: Yinxi Chen, Zongyun Chen, Brian Hii, Steven J. Miller

arxiv:2610.23992.title: Mathematics of Herding
arxiv:2610.23992.summary: A herd of animals often follows a leader who sets the direction of travel. The leader sometimes turns unexpectedly and the followers reshuffle. Yet the herd regroups itself and stays coherent.

arxiv:2610.23995.title: Extinction and the global structure of positive equilibria in a ratio-dependent intraguild predation model
arxiv:2610.23995.summary: We study an intraguild predation model with ratio-dependent trophic interactions. We first derive sufficient conditions for consumer extinction, total extinction, and global convergence to biologically relevant boundary equilibria. We then turn to coexistence at equilibrium and introduce a biologically motivated coordinate transformation that reduces the positive-equilibrium problem to an explicitly parameterized one-dimensional curve.

arxiv:2610.24022.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in $\mathbb{F}_2^7$
arxiv:2610.24022.summary: We prove that a nonempty subset of the binary vector space $\mathbb{F}_2^7$ is spectral if and only if it tiles $\mathbb{F}_2^7$ by translations. This is the smallest binary dimension left open by Ferguson and Sothanaphan. For the implication from tiling to spectrality we show that every eight-point subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^d$ admits $2^{d-3}$ frequencies whose pairwise differences avoid the zeros of its Fourier transform; consequently every tile of $\mathbb{F}_2^d$ with at least $2^{d-3}$ elements is spectral.

arxiv:2610.24025.title: New lower bounds for binary constant-weight codes from prescribed-automorphism search, and two quantum codes meeting their upper bounds
arxiv:2610.24025.summary: We give explicit binary constant-weight codes that raise the lower bounds on $A(n,6,w)$ in eight cells of Brouwer's table, all now listed there. The first round (9 October 2026) gave four values: $A(27,6,11)\ge 19305$, $A(27,6,12)\ge 24453$, $A(28,6,10)\ge 18642$ and $A(28,6,9)\ge 11154$, together with an explicit $A(24,6,12)$ code of 5566 words, now in the table's list of lost codes. The second round (14 October 2026) gave seven values, listed in the table since 15 October 2026: $A(29,6,10)\ge 27183$, $A(29,6,11)\ge 42042$, $A(29,6,9)\ge 14781$, $A(28,6,10)\ge 19110$, $A(27,6,12)\ge 24804$, $A(28,6,9)\ge 11388$ and $A(27,6,13)\ge 27783$, three of which replace first-round values.

arxiv:2610.24059.title: Sharp zero forcing numbers for the generalized Petersen graphs $P(n,3)$ and $P(n,4)$
arxiv:2610.24059.summary: We prove that $Z(P(n,3))=8$ for every $n\ge13$ and $Z(P(n,4))=10$ for every $n\ge18$, with both stabilization thresholds sharp, and give the exact values for all smaller admissible $n$. The first equality proves Krishnan's Conjecture 5; his Proposition 4 supplies its upper bound. The lower bounds use the external boundary of the first forcing sources: ten vertices have boundary at least eight in $P(n,3)$ for $n\ge14$, and sixteen vertices have boundary at least ten in $P(n,4)$ for $n\ge20$.
arxiv:2610.24059.authors: Arnav Krishnan, Haobo Ma, Wenlin Zhang

arxiv:2610.24080.title: An equiregular counterexample to the Sard conjecture for sub-Riemannian endpoint maps
arxiv:2610.24080.summary: Lerario, Rizzi and Tiberio disproved the sub-Riemannian Sard conjecture with a rank-two distribution on $\mathbb R^4$, of degree of nonholonomy five at the origin, whose endpoint map from that point has no regular values. Their distribution is neither equiregular nor real-analytic, and the equiregular case has remained open. We construct an equiregular rank-two distribution on an open set diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^9$, with small growth vector $(2,3,5,8,9)$, whose endpoint map from the origin has no regular values.

arxiv:2610.24083.title: Explicit formula for the Rasmussen invariant of odd pretzel knots
arxiv:2610.24083.summary: We compute the Rasmussen s-invariant for all odd pretzel knots, giving an explicit closed formula. The formula extends to all slice-torus invariants that are invariant under mutation. In the absence of mutation invariance, we prove the formula under a mild condition on the pretzel parameters, which we conjecture to be unnecessary.

arxiv:2610.24117.title: PArcK trees can get as hot as you want
arxiv:2610.24117.summary: We consider the combinatorial game Partizan Arc Kayles as a generalization of Domineering. An extensive technical search using genetic algorithms found hot positions of temperature exceeding 2. We discuss this search and construct a family of positions with high temperature that includes these graphs and prove that Partizan Arc Kayles has unbounded temperature.
arxiv:2610.24117.authors: Svenja Huntemann, Neil A. McKay, Craig Tennenhouse

arxiv:2610.24121.title: Sumsets regularity versus Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for monomial curves
arxiv:2610.24121.summary: Let $A=\{0=a_0<a_1<\dots<a_{k-1}=d\}$ be integers with greatest common divisor $1$, let $C_A$ be the projective monomial curve they define, and let $\mathrm{reg}(A)$ be the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of its coordinate ring. Gimenez and Gonz\'alez-S\'anchez proved $\mathrm{reg}(A)\le\sigma(A)+1$ for the sumsets regularity $\sigma(A)$; the reverse inequality $\sigma(A)\le\mathrm{reg}(A)$ was proposed as an open conjecture in a 2024 talk. We show that it fails and measure by how much.

arxiv:2610.24134.title: Invariants of big classes from asymptotic total Betti numbers
arxiv:2610.24134.summary: We introduce and study a new numerical invariant of big line bundles on normal complex projective varieties, defined in terms of the total Betti number of hypersurfaces associated with high tensor powers of the line bundle. We prove that this invariant is birational and provides an upper bound for the volume of the line bundle. When the big line bundle admits a rational Zariski decomposition, we show that the invariant coincides with the volume.

arxiv:2610.24143.title: The Kemeny-Braess Paradox in Random Graphs
arxiv:2610.24143.summary: In 2016, Kirkland and Zeng initiated the mathematical treatment of Braess paradox for random walks on graphs using Kemeny's constant as the measure of travel time. We study this phenomenon for the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graph $G(n,p)$. An edge in a connected graph is called Kemeny-Braess if its deletion preserves connectedness and decreases Kemeny's constant, while a nonedge is Kemeny-Braess if its insertion increases Kemeny's constant.
arxiv:2610.24143.authors: Manuel Bodirsky, Lorenzo Ciardo, Mihyun Kang

arxiv:2610.24145.title: Singular Aubry--Mather Sets for a Homogeneous Single-Input Control System
arxiv:2610.24145.summary: We develop an Aubry--Mather theory for the abnormal arcs of a time-minimal single-input affine control system in dimension three with homogeneous cubic drift. We show that the Bonnard--Kupka semi-invariant defining the abnormal locus is a Darboux polynomial of the desingularized singular field, with an explicit cofactor; this gives the invariance of the abnormal locus, a closed formula for the multiplier of its periodic components and, through the antipodal symmetry of the model, their description as lifts of ovals of a real plane quintic. For a compact invariant set of a singular flow we then define a singular Aubry--Mather structure, whose Lagrangian is supported on the graph of the…

arxiv:2610.24146.title: Energy of signed graphs and the vertex cover number
arxiv:2610.24146.summary: The energy $\mathcal{E}(\Gamma)$ of a signed graph $\Gamma=(G,\sigma)$ is the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix $A(\Gamma)$. In this article, we prove that $\mathcal{E}(\Gamma)\geq 2\tau(G)$, where $\tau(G)$ is the vertex cover number of $G$. The case of unsigned graphs, a 1980s conjecture proved only recently, is a special case of this result.
arxiv:2610.24146.authors: Aniruddha Samanta,  Deepshikha, Kinkar Chandra Das

arxiv:2610.24148.title: Strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Actions and Symmetric Chain Decompositions
arxiv:2610.24148.summary: We introduce a notion of a strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action on a poset, and conjecture the existence of such an action is equivalent to the existence of a symmetric chain decomposition of that poset. We explain the intuition behind the conjecture, go through a number of explicit examples, and prove some special cases and relaxations of the conjecture. Then we explain a computational experiment where we tested the conjecture on millions of randomly constructed rank-symmetric, rank-unimodal, and strongly Sperner posets.
arxiv:2610.24148.authors: Nate Harman, Rylan Rosas, Charles Troutman III, Chris Wu

arxiv:2610.24152.title: Geometric Stability of Dynamical Systems with Self-Generated State-Space Memory
arxiv:2610.24152.summary: We develop a geometric stability framework for dynamical systems coupled to memory fields generated by their own state trajectories.
